description: Canonical runtime DB data-plane contract. Table families, not individual rows, define ownership, data class, retention, deletion, and trust boundaries.

table_families.primary_access_path: Owner/requester-authenticated document-delivery facade under the existing Drive sharing namespace; request-bound copy approval, exact canonical connector-key binding, per-file channel fulfillment, activity and scoped revocation. Historical Drive requests retain their original path.
table_families.retention_policy: Active contracts have a finite access deadline. Abandoned preparation has a 30-minute lease bounded by that deadline; single-use possession challenges expire after five minutes; participant activity is retained at most 90 days. Retired cleanup purges selection, cached results, challenges and package envelopes after fencing. Account erasure removes public-key pins after fencing dependent requests. Financial provenance and unresolved storage inventory are retained separately.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Request-scoped workflow rows cascade only after independent cleanup inventory and opaque financial bindings preserve required obligations. Account deletion and expiry fence further release; no cascade is proof that provider objects are absent.
table_families.trust_boundary: One sign-in is not copy consent or payment. Exact A/B identity, selected files, terms/package digests, current authority and required channel receipts govern release. Public-key rows pin a request's canonical connector evidence; they are not a second key-registration authority. Selected filenames, provider IDs and revision metadata use existing encrypted Drive metadata custody. No file contents or unwrapped content/vault keys are stored here.
table_families.expected_row_growth: bounded contracts per owner/requester; at most 25 file receipts per contract; deduplicated paginated activity with 90-day retention and bounded idempotency/challenge records

table_families.primary_access_path: A device prepares PDF originals and watermark derivatives locally, then uploads bounded ciphertext through the qualified private GCS port. SQL binds immutable content generations, ciphertext hashes/object generations, encrypted metadata manifests and recipient/owner recovery wraps. B reads only through current paid entitlement and decrypts locally.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain approved ciphertext and wraps only while the finite delivery grant remains active. Keep uncertain writes and deletion fences until provider outcome is reconciled. Superseded staging follows its bounded lease; retained provider versions/soft deletion remain explicit pending destruction.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Deny access and fence admissions before exact-generation object deletion. Persist independent cleanup inventory across request/account cascades; verify bucket incarnation and provider-visible absence before removing it. Original Drive files are never modified or deleted by hosted-copy cleanup.
table_families.trust_boundary: AES-GCM content encryption and X25519 recipient wrapping happen on A's device. The metadata manifest contains no file keys or wraps. B's file-key envelopes are withheld before payment and until each required channel receipt; owner recovery is a separate owner-only path. The platform sees necessary access/payment metadata and ciphertext integrity only, not readable content or cryptographic proof of source fidelity.
table_families.expected_row_growth: at most 25 files and their qualified original/watermark renditions plus one metadata manifest per immutable generation; 4 MiB plaintext/rendition and 32 MiB total request ciphertext admission

table_families.primary_access_path: Existing signed payment/refund/payout reconciliation consumes one mode-aware delivery summary; independent ciphertext cleanup reconciles reserved, uncertain and exact-generation object outcomes after participant request erasure.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain minimal opaque financial mode/count/original paid-package binding under the existing payment obligation policy. Retain storage inventory only until all writer and provider-retention outcomes are reconciled. No unbounded recipient activity or personal document metadata is copied here.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Intentionally survives request/account cascades while a financial or provider-cleanup obligation exists. Preserve historical fulfillment before deleting content authority. A refund fence prevents later release; a lost provider response never proves erasure.
table_families.trust_boundary: Opaque request/object/operation identifiers, mode, counts, integrity and lifecycle receipts only. No raw participant identifiers, filenames, provider file IDs, content, credentials, vault keys or unwrapped file keys. Retained rows authorize reconciliation only, never a restored personal-content grant.
table_families.expected_row_growth: one financial binding per paid contract plus bounded inventory per staged ciphertext object, compacted after authoritative reconciliation

table_families.primary_access_path: vault setup, unlock-status, wrapper selection, account deletion, owner-bound One review completion, and explicit initial-signup Contacts lifecycle services
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while account exists; delete on account deletion or explicit vault reset flow.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Hard-delete with account deletion after dependent personal data is purged.
table_families.trust_boundary: Vault key material and wrappers remain encrypted or hashed; raw vault keys never persist server-side. Narrow vault_keys UI metadata exceptions one_business_profile_saved and one_magic_intelligence_saved are monotonic booleans set only after owner-confirmed PKM receipts; no research findings or profile facts are stored in these flags. Initial Contacts source, welcome acknowledgement and circle reference are bounded plaintext lifecycle metadata for explicitly enrolled new owners; no address book, credentials, research findings or PKM payload enters these fields. The circle reference is not encryption material and account deletion removes these fields with the vault row.

table_families.primary_access_path: account, persona, notification, verified email alias, and identity-cache services
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while account exists; refresh from authoritative identity sources where possible.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete or invalidate on account deletion; unregister push tokens on sign-out/delete.
table_families.trust_boundary: Metadata only; no vault keys, passphrases, tokens, or decrypted PKM.

table_families.primary_access_path: atomic full-account deletion, old-revision-compatible actor/vault root deletion triggers, Firebase bearer verification, catalog-installed tombstone guards for every public scalar user_id, role-prefixed *_user_id/user_<role>_id, firebase_uid, and *_firebase_uid reference, and an indexed hash-only account-state presence preflight
table_families.retention_policy: Retain one tombstone SHA-256 UID digest per deleted primary or validated phone-only cleanup UID to suppress resurrection, plus one monotonic SHA-256 presence marker per UID ever observed in a guarded account-state column so a legacy or rootless account is never later classified as a disposable phone session. Retain each raw Firebase UID and, for phone-orphan intents only, a domain-separated HMAC-SHA256 proof of the expected verified phone only while external identity cleanup is pending; scrub both on every terminal deleted, missing, or protected-identity outcome. Never persist the raw phone number or an unkeyed phone digest.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Tombstones are created by account deletion and deliberately survive it. The hash-only presence registry is backfilled transactionally when a versioned guard is installed and records the first later sighting of each UID; the phone-session preflight validates the complete live guard inventory and performs one indexed presence lookup rather than scanning user tables. READ COMMITTED writers take shared namespace-171 then namespace-198 UID advisory locks, reject writes after a matching tombstone, allow only unchanged or NULL-to-identity references, and reject non-NULL identity reassignment; deletion takes the corresponding exclusive locks. Remove lifecycle rows or database guards only through an audited, write-frozen operator procedure after proving that the external UID cannot authenticate or be restored.
table_families.trust_boundary: Deletion-suppression hash, short-lived keyed phone proof, intent kind, and bounded machine-safe cleanup metadata only; never email, raw phone number, unkeyed phone digest, token, provider profile, vault material, decrypted PKM, or exception messages.
table_families.expected_row_growth: one presence row per UID ever observed in guarded state, plus one tombstone row per deleted primary UID and at most one validated phone-only cleanup UID

table_families.primary_access_path: Feature-flagged personal-agent reservation, BYOC setup, provider provisioning, lifecycle replay, and the parked provider-deprovision intent design
table_families.retention_policy: Retain placement, setup and bounded recovery metadata while provider operations remain unresolved. Lifecycle events use the existing operational TTL. Required deletion tombstones and exact resource-absence/retention receipts survive removal until the governing erasure contract permits scrubbing; elapsed time never proves cleanup.
table_families.deletion_behavior: The owned erasure executor fences ordinary access, preserves retry custody and reconciles each captured resource before transactional finalization. Unconfirmed provider absence remains repairable. Account erasure cannot treat a suspended registry, destroyed key or accepted provider DELETE as complete resource cleanup.
table_families.trust_boundary: Owner-bound cloud coordinates, public keys, keyed phone hashes and bounded lifecycle receipts only. Provider credentials remain in existing encrypted custody or the admitted owner pod; never copy them into registry metadata.
table_families.expected_row_growth: one mutable registry and setup row per opted-in user, bounded 30-day lifecycle events, and parked deprovision intents that must not be activated without an owned consumer and compaction policy

table_families.primary_access_path: consent issuance, revocation, notification, and internal access review
table_families.retention_policy: Long-retention metadata audit; redact payload detail rather than deleting audit authority rows. The parked tamper-evident consent_audit_receipts chain needs explicit privacy/compliance approval for its raw subject_id retention or a chain-safe subject-redaction design before production activation.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account export may include safe audit metadata; deletion redacts user linkage only if legally required. Migration 201 explicitly treats consent_audit_receipts.subject_id as a raw Firebase/account UID, backfills it into the monotonic presence registry, and rejects post-tombstone receipt writes even while the retained chain awaits an approved redaction policy.
table_families.trust_boundary: Audit metadata only; signed-in is not consent and audit rows do not grant authority by themselves.

table_families.primary_access_path: The consent NOTIFY listener claims one key per consent_audit id (and per request notification sequence and TIMEOUT emission) with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING before sending a push, writing a delivery record, or ringing the requester's information_request_updated doorbell; the claim that returns a row owns the side effect across every worker and instance.
table_families.retention_policy: Pruned after 14 days by the consent timeout job.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Holds no user identifier (keys are consent_audit ids, request ids, or a SHA-256 digest), so account deletion has nothing to remove; rows age out with retention.
table_families.trust_boundary: Delivery key and claim time only. Grants no access and carries no scope, label, value, or person identifier.
table_families.expected_row_growth: one to three rows per consent event, bounded by the 14-day prune

table_families.primary_access_path: scoped export generation, connector key wrapping, and refresh jobs
table_families.retention_policy: Short-lived by export expiry; stale refresh jobs compacted after terminal status.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete on account deletion and expire/revoke when the consent grant expires.
table_families.trust_boundary: Encrypted export payloads and wrapped key metadata only; no raw export keys or decrypted PKM.

table_families.primary_access_path: PKM coherent snapshot, atomic store, owner rollback, delete-domain routes, and client-side vault unlock flows
table_families.retention_policy: Retain the first encrypted pre-v7 origin revision for the account lifetime; retain ordinary rollback revisions for 90 days; delete on account or explicit domain deletion.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete by user and domain for domain deletion; delete all user rows on account deletion.
table_families.trust_boundary: Ciphertext segments plus structural revision metadata only; backend does not inspect plaintext PKM payloads.

table_families.primary_access_path: AG-UI Agent One text chat, encrypted ADK session restore, encrypted legacy chat history restore, LLM context assembly, and owner-authenticated Magic discovery draft checkpoints (one.magic.discovery.v1/profile).
table_families.retention_policy: Chat persists while account exists or until user deletion. Magic discovery drafts expire after 24 hours; namespace-scoped hourly cleanup prunes up to 500 expired ciphertext rows without decrypting. Pending execution leases last 240 seconds and unavailable drafts have a 60-second retry cooldown; polling never extends retention.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete selected conversation rows with cascading encrypted messages; delete all user rows on account deletion; do not persist transient tool debug events.
table_families.trust_boundary: Session documents, command checkpoints, titles and messages persist as AES-GCM ciphertext sealed with the owner's chat key (HKDF-SHA256 of the vault key, label hussh-one-chat-v1), marked by the plaintext prefix hussh-chat-v1: and bound to their row. The browser sends only the derived key (X-Hussh-Chat-Key); the backend holds it in memory for that request and any bounded background run it started, with an absolute 300-second ceiling. Without it every read and write refuses; keys and owner tokens are never persisted. Platform-key rows from before the cutover are invisible to the code and deleted by migration 249. Pending connector reviews (one_mcp_pending_calls) are sealed the same way, bound to owner, conversation and handle, removed once the approved call has run, swept by the scheduled connector retention job when the review lapses, and erased on account reset and deletion. Frontend tool debug events remain live-only and are not stored.

table_families.primary_access_path: Firebase-authenticated Direct Messages service and /api/one/messages routes. Conversation creation and message insertion lock and verify only the canonical active connections pair; they never infer eligibility from Circle membership, trusted_connections, or a connection origin. Read paths remain participant-scoped after a connection ends.
table_families.retention_policy: Conversation-pair, directed block, and participant reaction metadata remain while both accounts exist. Ending a connection does not delete a conversation; it changes the write gate to read-only. A directed block remains until its blocker explicitly removes it or either account is deleted, including through a later reconnection.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Actor-profile foreign keys cascade conversation, directed block, and reaction rows on account deletion; message rows cascade from a deleted conversation and their reactions cascade with them. AccountService also removes the participant graph explicitly so no relationship history is retained for an erased account.
table_families.trust_boundary: Only canonical participant IDs, opaque UUIDs and timestamps are plaintext. RLS is default-deny with no client-table policies; authenticated routes/service enforce participant reads, block ownership and response shaping. The database trigger locks the canonical connection row and rejects new writes after revocation or either directed block, while history remains readable through the participant API.

table_families.primary_access_path: Participant-scoped conversation history and attachment reads, latest-message inbox projection, unread/read-receipt updates, sender-only edit and global delete actions, same-conversation replies, and transactionally committed recipient doorbells from the Direct Messages service.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain encrypted message history and attachments while its participant accounts exist. Disconnect and block preserve history but prohibit new message envelopes; no automatic disconnect deletion occurs. Attachments are limited to 5 MB each.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete attachments with their parent message, conversation, or either actor account through foreign-key cascades and AccountService account-erasure cleanup. A person can hide a message only from their own history; a sender can tombstone it for both participants. Never delete history merely because a connection is removed or blocked.
table_families.trust_boundary: Each text body and attachment is an AES-256-GCM envelope under server-managed DIRECT_MESSAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_V1. The GCM tag and AAD bind the conversation id, message id, and sender id; plaintext file bytes are never stored. Attachment reads require participant authorization and reject hidden or deleted messages. The transactional one_user_state_changed doorbell carries only opaque ids, time and a deep link, never content, cipher fields, sender identity or an unread count. This is encrypted-at-rest server-readable messaging, not client-key end-to-end encryption.

table_families.primary_access_path: Authenticated person-profile and Agent One workflows that prepare, create, inspect, cancel, expire, revoke, and export viewer-to-owner consent requests using opaque consumer scope references.
table_families.retention_policy: Pending bundles persist until resolved or expired; terminal bundle and item metadata remains only for the bounded consent-audit and replay window before compaction.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cancel pending bundles before account deletion where possible, then delete bundles and items where the deleting account is requester or owner; canonical consent audit receipts remain governed by their separate audit retention contract.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores requester/owner principals, opaque scope references, purpose, duration, status, and timestamps. It stores no requested information values, decrypted exports, vault keys, raw Firebase identifiers in consumer responses, or standing access; a pending request grants nothing.

table_families.primary_access_path: One action directive issuance, confirmation, exactly-once consumption, settlement, cancellation, and expiry
table_families.retention_policy: Short-lived authority metadata only; expire terminal and abandoned directives by expires_at and compact them after the replay window.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete all user rows on account deletion; otherwise remove expired rows after the bounded replay and audit window.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores generated action identifiers, revisions, state, timing, and keyed fingerprints only; never prompts, slots, credentials, consent exports, decrypted PKM, or protected information.

table_families.primary_access_path: Authenticated Agent One Capability Runtime start, resume, compare-and-set transition, and verified-settlement services shared by typed input, command voice, Siri handoff, web, and iOS. Browser and mobile callers reach it only through the authenticated backend API; they have no direct database role or row policy.
table_families.retention_policy: A run is non-authorizing at its bounded expires_at (24 hours by default). Active runs transition to expired on authoritative recovery; terminal and expired metadata remain only for the bounded replay and incident-review window before the authenticated maintenance path physically compacts expired parent runs in bounded batches. Encrypted task slots are workflow state, not durable personal memory or a transcript archive.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cascade-delete with the actor profile. Dependent workflow interaction, receipt, draft, and authorization rows cascade with their owned run where applicable; cancellation and expiry remove active authority rather than preserving a reusable mutation grant.
table_families.trust_boundary: Server-owned task authority with opaque run/capability identifiers, revision/state metadata, idempotency and settlement HMACs, and optional AEAD-encrypted bounded slots. It never stores raw audio, transcripts, routes or query strings, private entities, coordinates, addresses, credentials, provider payloads, or generated prose. RLS is default-deny and anon/authenticated database roles have no table access.

table_families.primary_access_path: PKM metadata, scope discovery, manifest repair, and replay/audit services
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while account exists; compact high-volume event metadata after replay window if safe.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete all user rows on account deletion; domain delete removes domain-scoped rows.
table_families.trust_boundary: Queryable metadata and scope handles only; no raw decrypted PKM.

table_families.primary_access_path: vault-owner profile controls publish safe public-profile projections; authenticated developer connectors read them by opaque handle through the public-profile export endpoint
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while the user keeps the section available by default; revoke or replace on posture change, projection refresh, domain deletion, or account deletion.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Soft revoke individual projections by setting revoked_at; hard-delete on account or domain deletion.
table_families.trust_boundary: Consumer-visible safe projection payloads only. Never raw encrypted PKM, pkm.read, workflow artifacts, hashes, provenance as shareable data, or broad blobs.

table_families.primary_access_path: client-side PKM cutover, server-issued upgrade claims, idempotent commit receipts, and generic PKM upgrade orchestration
table_families.retention_policy: Retain active and recent terminal runs; compact terminal rows after 30 days unless needed for incident review.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete all user rows on account deletion.
table_families.trust_boundary: Run, claim, revision, aggregate preservation, and commit metadata only; decrypt/transform/re-encrypt remains client-side after vault unlock.

table_families.primary_access_path: bounded legacy-to-PKM compatibility and account deletion cleanup only
table_families.retention_policy: No new canonical writes; delete after PKM cutover evidence proves no active dependency.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account deletion may remove legacy rows; new product features must not target these tables.
table_families.trust_boundary: Legacy ciphertext/metadata only; migration adapter remains time-boxed.

table_families.primary_access_path: legacy/domain reference compatibility during PKM scope migration
table_families.retention_policy: Retain until PKM manifests and scope registry fully replace runtime domain classification.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Reference cleanup only after migration plan; not user-delete scoped.
table_families.trust_boundary: Reference metadata only; not source of private PKM truth.

table_families.primary_access_path: RIA profile, marketplace deck actions, client relationship, bilateral connection-scope proposal, invite, and share-grant services
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while relationship/profile or deck lead exists; expire or disconnect relationship-scoped grants and preserve append-only scope-proposal audit metadata.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete or disconnect user-scoped relationships and marketplace deck actions on account/persona deletion.
table_families.trust_boundary: Professional and relationship metadata only; scope proposals contain opaque handles and capability lifecycle metadata, never decrypted investor PKM or an information export.

table_families.primary_access_path: RIA marketplace qualified investor deck, public discovery cards, and official SEC filing evidence
table_families.retention_policy: Refreshable public reference data; update from official public sources, preserve evidence URLs, and keep curation/admission fields plus replenisher run health auditable.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Not user-delete scoped; remove or correct only when the public-source inventory is withdrawn or superseded.
table_families.trust_boundary: Official/public investor reference records only; rows do not create signed-in marketplace users and are not connectable without opt-in.

table_families.primary_access_path: PublicProfileDiscoveryService exact canonical profile-URL reuse and the leased HusshOne acquisition worker; PostgreSQL GIN and semantic candidate retrieval are not connected to the current service.
table_families.retention_policy: Consent-gated, source-linked public findings may be retained for future exact-profile reuse. This release has no scheduled pool refresh or removal, and no existing-record import is allowed until source provenance and reuse permission are inventoried. The 100,000-profile target is not a measured capacity claim.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Shared pool rows do not cascade with a single owner's account or claim. No source-removal/suppression workflow is implemented in this release; broad reuse remains gated until pool correction and removal operations are defined and verified.
table_families.trust_boundary: Service-only shared public evidence. The public display-name anchor, public URLs, and source-linked findings are pooled after the v2 disclosure; login email, verified phone, employer/city hints, private corrections, and claim decisions are not shared pool fields.

table_families.primary_access_path: Firebase owner-scoped discovery status/start and vault-owner encrypted-draft/terminal-claim routes; PostgreSQL leased background worker and transactional Feed outbox.
table_families.retention_policy: One job per owner remains after claim to enforce the terminal one-time handoff until account deletion. Search hints are cleared after a ready profile, cancellation, or an unreviewable result; encrypted private drafts remain ciphertext only while the owner job exists. Transition and outbox rows are bounded by meaningful lifecycle changes.
table_families.deletion_behavior: AccountService hard-deletes the owner job, cascading its events and Feed outbox. The independent public evidence pool is retained and is not mutated by claim or account cleanup.
table_families.trust_boundary: Owner-scoped job state; prepared public findings are a pinned snapshot. Corrections and selected-card state are client-encrypted with the owner's vault key. Feed events contain generic status only; direct pool access is service-only.

table_families.primary_access_path: Atomic UTC-day acquisition and polling counters used by the background discovery worker's global budget guard.
table_families.retention_policy: Aggregate one row per UTC day with no owner identifier or query content; retained as a compact operational usage ledger. No scheduled compaction is configured in this release.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Not account-delete scoped; retain aggregate counts for capacity and cost review. An operator may remove old aggregate days under an approved retention policy.
table_families.trust_boundary: Aggregate counts only; no person identifier, anchor, provider response, profile finding, or credential.

table_families.primary_access_path: Read-only legacy receipt history during the private on-device Gmail cutover. New receipt sync and preview writes are blocked in the API and database.
table_families.retention_policy: Legacy receipt rows remain readable for continuity but receive no new writes. Terminal sync-run reads expire after 30 days; preview reads expire after seven days. Owner-scoped compaction remains available. The next cutover stage must replace this server cache with on-device Gmail pagination before an evidence-gated, owner-scoped purge and a separate destructive table-retirement migration.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Deletes remain permitted for Gmail disconnect and account deletion. No destructive bulk deletion occurs in this migration. The future purge must be owner-scoped, batched, reversible by encrypted PKM preservation evidence, and independently verified before the tables are dropped.
table_families.trust_boundary: Legacy provider-derived receipt summaries and preview artifacts are read-only. Trigger 265 blocks INSERT and UPDATE on the receipt and artifact tables, while API gates prevent new server-side Gmail receipt reads and summary creation.

table_families.primary_access_path: One owner-approved Gmail delivery prepare and final-send services; reviewed Gmail mailbox changes (archive, labels, read state, trash) proposed in One's chat and executed on the owner's confirmation
table_families.retention_policy: Prepared actions expire after ten minutes and are single-use. Required policy: retain terminal action metadata only for bounded delivery-state reconciliation, then compact it. A numeric terminal retention window and executable compaction process are not established by the current report-only registration. Mailbox-change proposals are unusable after ten minutes, deleted after execution, and purged (with failed ones) on the owner's next mailbox change. Scheduled sends (migration 275) wait until send_at, at most 30 days out, and stay sendable until send_at + 24 hours; the scheduled-mail drain sends a due row once, records a row past that window as failed (schedule_window_passed) and a row whose recipient disconnected as failed (recipient_disconnected), so the Feed keeps a lasting record of every unsent email, and clears payload_sealed and subject on every terminal state, with a bounded sweep of terminal scheduled rows at the start of each run. A voice cancel clears payload_sealed at once. Account reset deletes the owner's rows.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cascade-delete with the account owner; expired prepared actions are marked expired before reuse. Terminal metadata compaction without email-content retention remains required policy, not verified current enforcement. Mailbox-change proposals cascade-delete with the actor profile and are bound to the Gmail account they were resolved in, so a disconnect or account switch makes them unusable.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores only action identifiers, user identifiers, HMACs of normalized envelopes and idempotency keys, recipient counts, lifecycle timestamps, Gmail message/thread identifiers, and safe error codes for immediate, reply and voice draft sends; those rows never store recipient addresses, subject, body, OAuth tokens, vault credentials, PKM values, or One Email KYC mailbox information. Scheduled sends (migration 275) additionally store payload_sealed (AES-GCM under a key derived from the app signing key, with the owner and action bound as associated data; it holds the address, subject, body, the recipient's user id and the sending Google account subject, is opened only by the scheduled-mail drain at send time, and is cleared on cancel and on every terminal state) and two display-only plaintext columns, subject and recipient_display (the confirmed connection's name), shown in the owner's scheduled list on the owner's screen and never used as HMAC inputs. recipient_display may be spoken back to the owner by the Live model in the schedule and cancel confirmations, since it is the name the owner already said; subject and payload_sealed never reach the Live model. Every terminal scheduled row has payload_sealed and subject cleared; recipient_display stays for the owner's outcome notification. Mailbox-change proposals store only Gmail message and label identifiers, the bound Google account subject, the action and lifecycle state; never subject, sender, body or tokens.

table_families.primary_access_path: Email Agent opt-in personal Gmail monitor, owner review queue, and scheduled eligible-user scanner
table_families.retention_policy: Keep all monitor queue and scan-deduplication metadata for no longer than 30 days. Full Gmail messages and attachments are processed transiently and are never persisted by this workflow.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cascade-delete preferences, scan state, and workflow metadata with the vault owner. Turning monitoring off immediately deletes its queue and scan metadata, clears monitor coordination metadata, and blocks in-flight classification inserts.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores explicit monitoring preference, a monotonic opt-in generation, opaque Gmail History baseline/page-token/intra-page offset/lease metadata, Gmail provider identifiers, timestamps, classifier confidence, requested field labels, exact manifest leaf scope handles and segment identifiers, attachment-presence metadata, and keyed source/sender fingerprints. The history baseline is captured at opt-in so only later inbox messages are considered; the generation prevents stale scans from writing after consent changes. It never stores email subject/body/headers/addresses, attachment content, OAuth tokens, PKM values, decrypted exports, or generated drafts.

table_families.primary_access_path: Google OAuth connection service, owner/account-scoped additional Calendar credentials, confirmation-bound Calendar live-read/action service, and connected Schedule attendance review ledger
table_families.retention_policy: OAuth attempts expire after ten minutes. Calendar proposals are deleted after execution or failure and are unusable after ten minutes; the next Calendar mutation purges expired proposals. Provider credentials and grants remain only while the user keeps the service connected. Attendance review rows contain only submission metadata and redacted outcomes, expire after ten minutes, and are purged on the next review.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cascade-delete with the actor profile; service disconnect locally disables the relevant grant and removes its short-lived proposals. Account-level Google revocation is separate because it affects sibling services. Full account deletion snapshots the encrypted refresh token before erasure and, after commit, revokes it at Google best effort (account_deletion_provider_cleanup); a provider failure never rolls back the committed deletion.
table_families.trust_boundary: AES-GCM encrypted OAuth credential envelopes. The legacy provider row is the default identity; additional Calendar identities have separate account-bound encrypted envelopes and no Mail/Drive grants. No Calendar event cache or PKM projection is written.

table_families.primary_access_path: Cross-process state for Kai's long-running runs. kai_run_state (migration 253) holds one row per debate or portfolio-import run: the owning worker process writes a running row at start, refreshes a heartbeat and metadata-only progress every 5s and reads owner cancel requests in the same round trip, then writes a terminal receipt. Any process serves GET .../run/active, follows a run it does not hold to its end via GET .../run/{id}/stream, and records POST .../run/{id}/cancel. kai_analyze_runs (migration 125) is the earlier terminal-only checkpoint; migration 128 purges it on every replay and the runtime no longer writes it. On by default; KAI_ANALYZE_DURABLE_RUN_STORE=false is an emergency kill switch.
table_families.retention_policy: Rows carry expires_at (6h after the last heartbeat or the terminal write) and are deleted on every run start and every terminal write; a follower deletes relay ciphertext as soon as it reads it. Writes are coarse (start, one per 5s heartbeat, terminal), never per streamed frame, to respect the DB_SQLALCHEMY_MAX_OVERFLOW=0 pool pin.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete rows where the deleting account is the run owner (user_id) on account deletion; rows also self-expire via expires_at and are swept on run start and end.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores run identifiers, user_id, run kind, debate session id and ticker, status, timestamps, an event count with server-defined event and phase names, and a terminal receipt with a server-defined code. No holdings, statements, file names, decision cards, transcripts, model output, market material or PKM context. To hand the terminal frame to a different process for the same user, the requesting process stores only a one-time X25519 public key and keeps the private key in memory; the owner stores the frame sealed to it (X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 salted from the backend signing secret + AES-256-GCM, bound to run_id, user_id and both public keys) and the requester deletes it on read, or the owner when it stops answering, so it cannot be opened, forged or redirected from the database. All reads and writes are scoped by run_id and user_id.

table_families.primary_access_path: One Location Agent verified-recipient directory, server-owned and revocable automatic-approval preferences, owner-selected Save My Soul contacts, named-Circle join-code workflows, recipient public key registration, owner-approved grants, encrypted envelope writes, authenticated recipient ciphertext reads, the server-owned Location onboarding permission/GPS/place/Circle workflow, UAT-only short-lived nearby check-in with alias-based Connect requests, public request invites, Invite to One network onboarding, referrals, revocation, expiry, and metadata-only audit
table_families.retention_policy: One mutable standing-rule metadata row is retained while the account exists, including the latest disabled state and version needed to invalidate stale clients. Active grants and ciphertext envelopes are short-lived by scoped duration; expired or terminal workflow rows are retained only for bounded operational review before compaction. Location onboarding leases, opaque receipts, pre-vault draft metadata, and PKM-finalize authorities expire with their task. Drafts and unused authorities are removed on sign-out, cancellation, finalization, or expiry; expired parent-run compaction cascades the remaining run-scoped workflow records, and none can authorize a later run.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete standing automatic-approval and visibility preferences plus rows where the deleting account is owner, excluded party, nearby attendee, SMS contact, recipient, requester, referrer, referred or candidate user, join-code creator, or key owner; remove visibility exclusions before their owner preference, revoke active grants, nearby presence, and join codes before deletion where possible, and cascade every onboarding lease, receipt, draft, and finalize authority through its owner-bound capability run.
table_families.trust_boundary: Raw live-share coordinates remain on owner and recipient devices. Standing automatic-approval preferences contain only enabled state, scope, Circle identifier, server activation time, and rule version; every automatic grant locks and revalidates that rule and the current relationship. UAT nearby presence captures a fresh point at confirmation and stores that point only as short-lived AES-256-GCM ciphertext plus a six-hour server-keyed spatial candidate token; accuracy is request-memory-only. Checkout clears point material synchronously. Expiry synchronously blocks roster and Connect access; the next feature operation or required hosted hourly retention job scrubs the due envelope and token. Backend also stores recipient public keys, grant metadata, ciphertext envelopes, keyed join-code digests, rotating nearby participant aliases, public invite token hashes, Invite to One token hashes, One Network connection metadata, request metadata, hashed public-intake throttling metadata, and audit metadata. Onboarding records add only allowlisted workflow and interaction enums, opaque owner/run/revision identifiers, timestamps, and HMAC/SHA digests; the actual pre-vault Location payload remains encrypted on the same device. It must not persist nearby point plaintext, exact distance, plaintext venue labels or addresses, map previews, movement trails, raw public tokens, raw Circle codes, audio, transcripts, route queries, place labels, device-draft ciphertext, or keys. Nearby rosters require mutual active opt-in, expose no stable user id or peer location, and remain disabled in production. Circle code resolution reveals only a safe name, owner label, member count, and expiry.

table_families.primary_access_path: Short-lived ledger of completed nearby check-in visits, so the place a person just left can be rated and so the check-in travel-continuity guard survives a checkout that clears the presence anchor. The venue is readable only as an AES-256-GCM envelope bound by AAD to its owner, alongside a server-keyed equality token that allows same-venue and distinct-place checks without decryption.
table_families.retention_policy: Each visit expires seven days after check-in and is deleted by the Location retention purge on its own expires_at, independently of the twelve-hour window used for terminal presence rows.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Rows cascade on actor_profiles deletion and are also deleted explicitly by the account service for the owning user.
table_families.trust_boundary: backend_runtime

table_families.primary_access_path: One 1-5 star rating per person per place, private to its author and readable only by them, plus an anonymous per-place count and sum derived from those rows. This is the only durable person-to-venue link in One Location and is created solely on acceptance of the named, versioned consent one-location-place-rating-v1. It stores no review text, no author display identity, and no author reference reaches any cross-user projection; the aggregate holds no user reference at all and is withheld below five raters and reported in buckets.
table_families.retention_policy: A rating is retained while the account exists and is updated in place on a revisit. The aggregate is derived state, recomputed from the surviving rows on every insert, update and delete.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Ratings cascade on actor_profiles deletion and are deleted explicitly by the account service, which recomputes every affected place aggregate in the same statement -- an average that still counts a deleted rating has not deleted it.
table_families.trust_boundary: backend_runtime

table_families.primary_access_path: One referral program: server-minted public attribution slugs, pre-authentication attribution records bound to a canonical user only after sign-in, one referrer-to-referred relationship per referred user, server-calculated agent engagement sessions, an append-only idempotent event ledger, versioned qualification policy, and the human risk-review queue. Read by the Profile Referrals tab as aggregate counts and status words only. Migration 270 adds the gamification layer built on top of this graph: versioned program settings (points, milestones, streaks, flash windows, weekly schedule, prize catalogue) and the weekly reward round schedule slots. Migration 271 adds cumulative scoring: an append-only points ledger (one_referral_score_events), a durable worker queue enqueued atomically alongside each qualification transition (one_referral_scoring_jobs), a per-referrer streak-award watermark (one_referral_streak_state, recomputed from relationship qualification dates rather than stored incrementally), and published cumulative-ranking snapshots (one_referral_leaderboard_snapshots / _entries) the dashboard reads instead of a live aggregate query. Migration 272 adds circles and milestones: an interval history of each user's single active referral-contest team (one_referral_circle_selections, new and referral-owned -- it never writes to one_location_circles or one_location_circle_memberships), an append-only settled-once record of which team gets credit for each qualified relationship resolved at event time (one_referral_circle_contributions, COUNT(*) per circle_id is the team's raw cumulative score), lifetime once-only milestone entitlements (one_referral_milestone_entitlements), and a staff review/fulfillment foundation with no shipping or purchase capability (one_referral_fulfillment_records). Migration 273 adds one_referral_display_handles: an opt-in, self-chosen public alias distinct from actor_identity_cache.display_name, so a referrer who has not set one has no public leaderboard identity and is rendered as an anonymous placeholder rather than their real/account name. Migration 274 adds one_referral_weekly_awards: finalized weekly rank-1/2/3 prize awards, unique on (reward_round_id, award_slot) only -- deliberately never on user_id, because the program is cumulative with no weekly reset and a previous winner is expected to win again in a later round without earning anything new that week. cumulative_points_at_cutoff is a frozen snapshot written once at finalization; winning never writes back to one_referral_score_events, so a prize is never itself a point award, and re-running finalization for an already-finalized round is a no-op via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on that same unique pair. Migration 347 separates referral points and loyalty coins, replaces the historical referral-date streak interpretation with atomic per-owner calendar-day app attendance, adds immutable inherited referral-network membership with late-parent subtree reconciliation, records real completed One ADK replies as content-free transactional usage events, and exposes owner-scoped direct-member display names plus reward claim state. Published individual rank uses coins; referral-network circle rank uses qualified descendant counts independently of Location Circle permissions. Migration 348 credits the current atomic Memory save through confirmed pkm_events content_write provenance, excluding upgrade, projection and maintenance events and sharing the legacy once-per-owner/day reward key.
table_families.retention_policy: Pending attributions expire with the policy attribution window and are swept. Relationships and their event ledger are retained for the life of the referrer's account as the audit trail behind a public count. Engagement sessions are closed or abandoned once their heartbeat gap passes and are retained only long enough to reconcile a qualification decision. Program settings versions and reward rounds are program-level configuration and schedule state, not per-user data, and are retained indefinitely as the program's own audit trail of what rules and schedule were live when. Score events are an append-only, never-updated ledger retained for the life of the referrer's account (points are never deducted except by an audited reversal row); scoring jobs and the streak watermark are operational/derived state retained alongside it; leaderboard snapshots are retained as the published history of what the ranking looked like at each publish. Circle selections, circle contributions, and milestone entitlements are retained for the life of the referrer's account as the audit trail behind team and milestone standing; fulfillment records are retained as the review/shipment audit trail for each entitlement. Weekly awards are retained indefinitely as the audit trail of who won which round, their frozen cumulative standing at that moment, and who reviewed/fulfilled the prize. Daily attendance has one row per owner and configured calendar day, retained for the account lifetime; network membership has one row per owner, retained while that owner exists. Neither is imported into personal Live Memory: these are operational rewards and referral workflow records, surfaced through the owner-authorized referral dashboard. No prompt, answer, key, or decrypted session state is stored in usage events.
table_families.deletion_behavior: AccountService handles the migration-165 graph explicitly before deleting actor_profiles: risk reviews and events, then every relationship involving the referrer, referred user, or their owned/bound attribution, then those attributions, owned codes, and engagement sessions. This order is mandatory because relationship.attribution_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT while bound_user_id is ON DELETE SET NULL; relying on the actor cascade can roll back deletion or retain a departed user's attribution. The referrer's public count is derived from surviving relationships, so it falls accordingly. A partial migration-165 table set fails closed instead of deleting the account spine. one_referral_program_settings and one_referral_reward_rounds carry no actor_profiles foreign key -- they are global program configuration and schedule state, not one referrer's or one referred user's data -- so account deletion never touches them and they are deliberately absent from the walk above. one_referral_score_events, one_referral_scoring_jobs, one_referral_streak_state, one_referral_leaderboard_snapshot_entries, one_referral_circle_selections, one_referral_circle_contributions, one_referral_milestone_entitlements, one_referral_display_handles, and one_referral_weekly_awards each reference actor_profiles(user_id) ON DELETE CASCADE and are brought under install_account_deletion_write_guards() (migration 201) by their own migration's refresh call, so a write referencing a tombstoned account is rejected the same way the migration-165 tables already are; none of them are yet in AccountService's explicit pre-deletion walk, so deletion itself still relies on the CASCADE rather than an audited ordered delete the way the migration-165 relationship graph has. one_referral_fulfillment_records has no actor_profiles reference of its own; it cascades transitively through its entitlement's deletion. Migration 347 corrects bound-attribution deletion to CASCADE and adds the new attendance, network circle/member tables to the existing account-deletion write-guard installer. Attendance and memberships reference actor_profiles ON DELETE CASCADE. When an account is deleted, the referral-network trigger detaches its direct children and rebuilds surviving rooted chains in the same transaction, retaining their valid independent descendant memberships. Earned owner awards and claim state remain unchanged by migration/replay/behavioral rollback, but account-owned records follow existing account-deletion cascades.
table_families.trust_boundary: The slug is public and is never a credential: resolving one proves nothing about who holds it, and the referred user still signs in through the existing identity flow. Installation and network signals are stored only as salted hashes for abuse velocity, never raw and never returned to any client. Internal risk reason codes never reach a user-facing surface.

table_families.primary_access_path: Authenticated One Location People-tab Circle creation, code join, targeted existing-direct-connection invitation and acceptance, membership listing, removal, leave, and deletion workflows. Code join or targeted-invite acceptance creates source-aware canonical mutual connection origins with every active Circle member; creating a targeted invitation alone creates no membership or connection.
table_families.retention_policy: Active memberships persist while the Circle exists. Pending targeted invitations are marked expired opportunistically after their bounded invitation window. Accepted, declined, cancelled, and expired targeted invitations are compacted by the scheduled One Location terminal-work retention endpoint after its bounded retention window, and are deleted immediately with the Circle or either account. Left, removed, and deleted membership state otherwise remains for bounded reconciliation before compaction.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete owned Circles and every invitation or membership referencing the deleting account. Before Circle hard deletion or membership exit, revoke only that Circle's active connection origins, recompute the canonical connection, and explicitly delete the revoked Circle origins; the source-Circle foreign key restricts bypassing this lifecycle. Preserve direct, imported, legacy-invite, or other-Circle origins. Reassign Circle-sourced active location grants to a surviving direct or other-Circle relationship and revoke them only when no eligible relationship remains.
table_families.trust_boundary: Joining a named Circle creates mutual connection metadata but never creates a trusted_connections edge, SMS selection, location grant, capability token, envelope, coordinate, or map projection. Existing direct connections require a targeted Circle invitation and invitee acceptance before membership. Location and Save My Soul authority remain separate explicit user actions.

table_families.primary_access_path: Vault-owner session bootstrap ensures a missing Wallet Profile from account basics, and owner controls edit, pause, resume, rotate, and revoke one card per account; the Apple Wallet pass and the public /c/{token} page resolve that card unauthenticated by SHA-256 hash of the presented share token, through the same projection builder the owner's preview-as-visitor uses
table_families.retention_policy: Retain one row while the owner keeps a card; a revoked card is retained as a tombstone so an already-printed QR can answer honestly, and is hard-deleted on account deletion or reset.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Soft revoke by setting status='revoked' and revoked_at, which invalidates the share token immediately; hard-delete on account deletion or reset, before actor_profiles tears down the identity spine.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores allowlisted account basics for automatic creation and subsequent owner-selected card fields (name, username, headline, organisation, coarse location label, summary, skills, contact links), the SHA-256 token digest, an optional owner/digest-bound AES-GCM token recovery envelope, and aggregate scan counters. Plaintext share tokens are never stored. Only the authenticated matching owner can recover a token; automatic provisioning never overwrites existing fields or reactivates paused/revoked profiles. No per-scan rows, IP addresses, user agents, geolocation, or referrers are recorded. The card grants no vault, PKM, or marketplace access, and is deliberately not published through pkm_default_available_projections.

table_families.primary_access_path: One Information Marketplace access-request inbox: a buyer files a request for owner-approved access to a published data-slice safe projection; the owner lists, approves, or denies server-side from the marketplace surface or via Agent One over A2A.
table_families.retention_policy: Pending requests are retained until resolved; approved, denied, or expired rows are retained only for bounded operational and consent-audit review before compaction.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete rows where the deleting account is the owner (or the buyer once buyer identity exists); resolve pending requests to a terminal status before deletion where possible.
table_families.trust_boundary: Backend stores only request metadata (owner and buyer references, slice domain, scope handle, label, price, status, timestamps). It never stores raw PKM values; a request grants no access on its own and only the safe-summary projection is ever shared after explicit owner approval.

table_families.primary_access_path: One marketplace Owner tab: the owner creates, prices and lists packets (named bundles of their own PKM scope references) for sale; hussh.ai White Pages reads only the titles and prices of a verified owner's for-sale packets through the public listing lookup.
table_families.retention_policy: Retained while the owner keeps the packet; deleting a packet removes its row.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete every row for the owner on account reset and account deletion.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores packet titles, prices and PKM scope references ({domain, scopeHandle, label}) only. It never stores a PKM value; a sale moves data only through an owner-approved marketplace request sealed to the buyer's key.

table_families.primary_access_path: hussh.ai White Pages 'Is this you?' claim: a signed-in, phone-verified One user claims a public-record listing id; an operator verifies it; the public listing lookup then shows the verified owner's for-sale packets.
table_families.retention_policy: Active claims are retained while pending or verified; withdrawn and rejected claims are retained only for bounded operational review.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete every row for the user on account reset and account deletion, returning the listing to unclaimed.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores the user reference, the public listing id and name, status and timestamps. The public lookup never returns a user id.

table_families.primary_access_path: hussh.ai White Pages buy flow: a signed-in buyer pays hussh for one packet through Stripe Checkout; the signed Stripe webhook marks the order paid and files an owner-approved marketplace access request; denied, expired or orphaned requests are refunded by the packet-order reconcile.
table_families.retention_policy: Retained while payment or refund is unsettled and for bounded financial and consent-audit review afterwards; snapshots the packet title and price paid.
table_families.deletion_behavior: On account deletion, paid but undelivered orders move to refund_pending, are refunded in full by the reconcile, and the row is then deleted; all other rows (unpaid, settled, or delivered) are deleted, and an owner earning not yet transferred is forfeited.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores buyer and owner references, the public listing id, packet id and title, amounts, status and Stripe object ids. No card data (Stripe-hosted Checkout) and no PKM values. Orders record Stripe mode; provider operations require the current matching mode, while unresolved historical mode remains legacy and fails closed.

table_families.primary_access_path: hussh.ai credits plans: a buyer subscribes monthly through Stripe Checkout; the signed webhook grants the plan's credits once per paid invoice (pkm_grant_credits, expiring the unused balance) and records plan status; buying a packet with credits spends from the ledger (pkm_spend_credits under a per-user advisory lock); refunds of credit-paid orders return credits.
table_families.retention_policy: Subscription row retained while the plan exists; ledger rows are append-only and retained for the life of the account for balance and audit.
table_families.deletion_behavior: On account deletion the ledger is deleted and the subscription row is deleted after its Stripe subscription id is moved to pkm_credit_subscription_cancellations for cancellation.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores user references, plan, Stripe customer and subscription ids, status, period end, and integer credit deltas with idempotency refs. No card data and no PKM values.

table_families.primary_access_path: Account deletion moves a deleted subscriber's Stripe subscription id here; the scheduled work drain cancels it at Stripe and deletes the row.
table_families.retention_policy: Transient: deleted as soon as the Stripe cancellation succeeds.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Holds no user identity; rows are removed by the drain after cancellation.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stripe subscription id and timestamp only; no user id.

table_families.primary_access_path: Profile Payouts and marketplace owner payouts use stripe_owner_payout_accounts keyed by owner and Stripe test/live mode. Stripe-hosted Express onboarding collects bank and identity details. The legacy pkm_owner_payout_accounts mapping remains for rolling compatibility and is adopted only after provider verification under the current mode key.
table_families.retention_policy: Retained while the owner keeps their account; at most one current mapping per owner and Stripe mode, plus the legacy compatibility row until its separately reviewed retirement.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account reset and deletion remove both current-mode mappings and the legacy mapping after settlement obligations retain their previously verified destination. The Stripe Express account itself is held by Stripe.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores user reference, explicit test/live mode, Stripe Connect account ID and readiness flags only. Never substitute an account across modes. Bank and identity details stay with Stripe. Postgres is authoritative; any future Redis readiness cache must preserve owner-plus-mode keys and signed-event invalidation and cannot authorize settlement.

table_families.primary_access_path: One Information Marketplace end-to-end slice delivery: a buyer publishes an ECDH recipient public key (private half stays on the buyer device); on owner approval the seller device seals the requested safe-summary slice against that key and posts a ciphertext envelope, which the buyer fetches and decrypts locally from the Received-data surface.
table_families.retention_policy: Recipient public keys persist per buyer while active; delivery envelopes are retained for the scoped access duration and are best-effort deleted on revoke, with terminal rows retained only for bounded operational review before compaction.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete rows where the deleting account is the key owner (buyer) or the envelope owner/recipient; delete delivered ciphertext on revoke where possible.
table_families.trust_boundary: Backend stores only recipient public keys, sealed ciphertext envelopes, and delivery metadata. It holds no private keys and never stores raw PKM values or plaintext slices; only the safe-summary projection is ever sealed, and the server acts as a blind relay that cannot decrypt.

table_families.primary_access_path: Generalized directional trusted-connection graph. Written only via Agent One (add/remove/list intents delegated to the agent_connections lane) and via circle-invite claim (one-way claimerâ†’inviter edge); read in-process by any backend agent (e.g. Location, Email) through TrustedConnectionsService for SOS recipient resolution and check-in targeting. People are resolved read-only through the One Location verified-recipient directory. Supersedes the former one_location_network_connections table; its forward-only removal is pending live row-count, retention, and backup preflight.
table_families.retention_policy: Active directed edges persist as the owner's relationship graph; revoked edges are retained only for bounded operational review before compaction.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete rows where the deleting account is the owner or the trusted user; revoke active edges before deletion where possible.
table_families.trust_boundary: Backend stores only connection metadata (owner and trusted-user references, status, source, resolution method, optional label, timestamps). It stores no raw contact identifiers, coordinates, or PKM values, and a connection grants no data access on its own.

table_families.primary_access_path: Two-way mutual connection graph. connection_requests holds the directional handshake; connections is the canonical pair projection; connection_origins is the durable source ledger for direct requests, legacy invites, imports, viewer-relative contact_sync provenance, and one or more named Circles. Contact sync uses the visible verified-phone Connect-directory default under contact_directory_auto_connect_v2, honors explicit contact opt-out and marketplace hide, revalidates each submitted digest against the current unique verified phone, and writes every eligible non-suppressed match as canonical graph projections transactionally. Policy writers and graph activation share a per-user database lock. Viewer-relative provenance records the directory policy and actual preference state without fabricating historical consent evidence. contact_sync_lookup_budgets is the Postgres-authoritative cross-instance abuse-budget seam; SlowAPI is only the outer request-count guard. Named Circle join/accept writes only named_circle origins. The canonical pair remains active while any origin is active.
table_families.retention_policy: Active origins keep their canonical connection active. Revoked canonical connection rows persist for the lifetime of either account because they are the durable disconnect-suppression tombstone that prevents contact sync from resurrecting a relationship; an explicit request/accept may reactivate them. Revoked origins and terminal requests may be compacted under their bounded operational policy without deleting that canonical tombstone. Lookup-budget buckets contain counts only and are pruned after two days on the next sync by that user.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete rows where the deleting account is either party. Membership leave/removal/Circle deletion revokes only the matching named_circle origins and recomputes each canonical pair; direct and other-Circle origins survive. connection_origins cascade when their canonical connection is deleted. AccountService explicitly deletes contact_sync_lookup_budgets; the table deliberately has no vault FK so a Firebase-authenticated pre-vault account is handled by explicit route policy rather than an incidental constraint failure.
table_families.trust_boundary: Backend stores only connection and source-provenance metadata (user references, Circle reference, status, source, optional plaintext message on a direct request, timestamps) plus aggregate lookup counts. It stores no contact hash, phone digits, or address-book rows. A connection or contact/Circle origin grants no location access, automatic all_contacts approval, SMS selection, capability, envelope, coordinate, PKM value, or information access on its own.

table_families.primary_access_path: First-party Hermes device registration, listing, proof-of-possession lookup, last-used and last-synced tracking, revocation, advisory remote-revoke seal telemetry, and advisory liveness heartbeats through TrustedDeviceService.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain active device registrations while the account exists; retain revoked metadata only for bounded security review before compaction.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete all device rows on account deletion; explicit device revocation immediately disables new challenges and records the revocation timestamp.
table_families.trust_boundary: Public P-256 device keys and device metadata only, including PKM device-sync cursors, remote-revoke seal timestamps, and device-reported liveness heartbeats reduced to an allow-list of runtime scalars (machine identifier, configured model, busy flag, active session count, next cron run); never private keys, Firebase tokens, vault passphrases, vault keys, decrypted PKM, filesystem paths, or developer credentials.

table_families.primary_access_path: Short-lived PKCE authorization codes and single-use proof-of-possession challenges consumed atomically through TrustedDeviceService.
table_families.retention_policy: Authorization and challenge rows expire within minutes; consumed and expired rows are compacted after the bounded replay-investigation window.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete all user-bound rows on account deletion; revocation prevents new challenges and existing challenges remain unusable after expiry or first consumption.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores hashes, public device keys, redirect metadata, opaque identifiers, and expiry/consumption timestamps only; no bearer tokens, private device keys, vault secrets, decrypted PKM, or raw nonce values.

table_families.primary_access_path: Metadata-only trusted-device authorization, challenge, capability issuance, use, and revocation audit events written by TrustedDeviceService.
table_families.retention_policy: Long-retention security audit metadata; compact only under the regulated audit-retention policy and redact optional metadata before deleting authority history.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account export may include safe event metadata; hard-delete user-linked runtime audit rows on account deletion unless a separate legally mandated retention system owns an immutable copy.
table_families.trust_boundary: Event type, user/device references, timestamps, and allowlisted metadata only; never authorization codes, nonce values, signatures, tokens, private keys, vault secrets, or decrypted information.

table_families.primary_access_path: Cross-instance one-time nonce registry for signed One voice relay tickets (migration 084). consume_relay_ticket_shared() in api/routes/one/relay_auth.py enforces single use globally via INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; a conflicting insert means replay. Expired rows are pruned opportunistically by expiry scan. Scale-plane doctrine: Postgres now, Redis SETNX-with-TTL later behind the same seam.
table_families.retention_policy: Rows live only for the ticket validity window (about 60 seconds); expired nonces are pruned opportunistically on subsequent consumption calls.
table_families.deletion_behavior: No per-account rows exist; nothing to delete on account deletion. Rows self-expire and are pruned by expiry.
table_families.trust_boundary: Backend stores only an opaque random nonce and its expiry timestamp. No user identifiers, personal information, tokens, or coordinates are stored; a row grants no access and only prevents ticket replay.

table_families.primary_access_path: One Information Marketplace proactive opportunity nudges: the server derives dateless intent signals from the owner's publishable-slice metadata (and the client may post dated expiry signals), surfaced as flashcards on Agent One where the owner publishes, snoozes, or dismisses them; state is read and mutated server-side per owner.
table_families.retention_policy: One durable row per owner+dedupe_key; snoozed rows reappear the next day, published/dismissed/expired rows are retained for lifecycle idempotency and bounded operational review before compaction.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete rows where the deleting account is the owner (user_id); no cross-account references exist.
table_families.trust_boundary: Backend stores only safe signal metadata (title, body, domain, scope handle, suggested price, nudge lifecycle state, timestamps) derived from summary projections. It never stores raw PKM values; dated expiry details are client-derived and posted as safe summaries only.

table_families.primary_access_path: market/reference lookup, cache refresh, and Kai market insight services
table_families.retention_policy: Refreshable shared reference/cache data; expire market cache by freshness windows.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Not user-delete scoped; rebuild from providers or seed/reference sources.
table_families.trust_boundary: Shared market/reference data only; no user-private PKM.

table_families.primary_access_path: One mailbox intake, account-scoped automatic-preparation preference, KYC workflow status, per-user public client connector metadata, consent continuation, transient approved Gmail send, and encrypted PKM writeback receipt
table_families.retention_policy: Active workflow metadata retained while open; legacy dev/UAT draft_body rows are redacted by migration and terminal metadata is compacted by retention jobs.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete user-linked workflows on account deletion; keep mailbox watch state without user data.
table_families.trust_boundary: Metadata only plus public connector metadata and send/writeback hashes; no raw full email threads, connector private keys, consent export plaintext, vault contents, broad decrypted PKM, or review draft plaintext. Approved outgoing email body may be handled transiently only for Gmail send and must not be logged or persisted.

table_families.primary_access_path: Profile Connected Systems and Agent CRM proposal approval flows, including encrypted-fields request envelopes and local-owner approval
table_families.retention_policy: Pending intents may retain the allowlisted CRM payload required to execute an approved write; terminal rows retain field names, ids, status, and sanitized result summaries only. CRM-ZK contexts and approval challenges expire or are consumed and are compacted promptly. Record bindings retain active and disconnected external CRM record pointers with workflow metadata so recovery does not erase linkage history.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete user-linked workflow rows on account deletion; compact terminal rows after the operational review window.
table_families.trust_boundary: External CRM handoff is outside the Hussh encrypted-fields boundary when plaintext is sent to Salesforce. crm-encrypted-fields.v1 rows hold only recipient public-key metadata, encrypted field envelopes, hashes, and approval metadata; browser and MuleSoft handle field values, Hussh never decrypts them. Scrub terminal payload values.

table_families.primary_access_path: Connected Systems read/create/update approval audit, owner-confirmed local disconnect, and CRM readback result classification
table_families.retention_policy: Retain metadata audit rows for operational review; never retain raw CRM request, MCP result, or readback payload values in audit events.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Preserve regulated audit metadata where required; redact user linkage if account deletion or legal process requires it.
table_families.trust_boundary: Metadata-only audit evidence for external CRM actions. No vault data, raw PKM, full CRM payloads, credentials, or MCP tokens.

table_families.primary_access_path: Connected Systems CRM-ZK owner public-key registration, signature verification, rotation, and revocation
table_families.retention_policy: Retain the active public signing-key metadata while the owner connection is active; retain retired/revoked metadata only for the bounded operational and audit review window.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete user-linked key metadata on account deletion and mark keys revoked before connector disconnection completes.
table_families.trust_boundary: Public SPKI, algorithm, status, and fingerprint metadata only. The owner private signing key remains device-local and is never stored or reconstructed by the service.

table_families.primary_access_path: Operator CRM registry validation, activation, update, and deactivation audit trail.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain configuration fingerprints, revisions, capability names, validation outcomes, and sanitized summaries for operational and security review; never retain decrypted credentials or provider response payloads.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Operator-managed audit evidence is not user-delete scoped; redact operator linkage only when required by access-governance or legal policy.
table_families.trust_boundary: Metadata-only evidence for registry administration. No client credentials, access tokens, CRM records, vault material, PKM information, or raw validation responses.

table_families.primary_access_path: Historical recipient-key metadata retained solely for completed CRM-ZK and CRM-ZK-UAT workflow history; no active runtime, route, or registry loader reads these tables.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain non-secret public-key and lifecycle metadata only for the bounded operational and audit review window; no new rows are created after profile retirement.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Operator-managed historical reference metadata; do not delete rows needed to explain completed intents or audit records. Purge only under the approved retention process.
table_families.trust_boundary: Public key, fingerprint, profile, environment, and lifecycle metadata only. No private keys, CRM credentials, record values, ciphertext envelopes, or owner information.

table_families.primary_access_path: DB-backed Connected Systems resolution: gateway URL, per-operation MCP tool catalog, and pinned CRM encrypted-fields recipient public-key registry for enterprise CRM integrations (replaces hardcoded ConnectedSystemDefinition)
table_families.retention_policy: Retain active enterprise CRM integration config, per-operation tool catalog, and recipient public-key records while the integration is provisioned; retire or revoke keys and deactivate the registry rather than delete active history.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Operator-managed reference config; not user-delete scoped. crm_operation_endpoints cascade-delete with their parent crm_id.
table_families.trust_boundary: MuleSoft bearer rows contain no CRM credentials: gateway authentication is process secret configuration and CRM credentials remain in MuleSoft. Header-auth rows retain encrypted legacy credentials. Recipient public keys and fingerprints are non-secret verification material. Gateway URLs are non-secret config. No raw long-lived secrets at rest.

table_families.primary_access_path: Connected Systems provider-schema catalogue and mapper caches for a CRM object schema fingerprint and the tool-less field-role proposal used by verified-identity lookup and create-field selection.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain catalogue rows only through their bounded fresh/stale windows and ready mappings through their 24-hour TTL; invalidate immediately when the registry revision or CRM schema changes, or when schema validation fails. These caches rebuild from the active provider and are never durable user memory.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Not user-delete scoped. Rows cascade-delete with the provisioned CRM registry row and can be invalidated without affecting CRM records or user bindings.
table_families.trust_boundary: Public CRM schema metadata and normalized field-role keys only. Never store CRM records, verified profile values, record IDs, credentials, consent/vault material, prompts, telemetry plaintext, or unvalidated model output.

table_families.primary_access_path: Owner-authenticated selection/management and separately consented continuous live collection discovery, with durable connection-generation-bound ingestion leases and versioned publication. No client database access.
table_families.retention_policy: Keep encrypted source metadata and current preview chunks while the connection generation remains active. Complete original-document pages and semantic evidence are versioned in the continuous evidence family. Successful preview publication replaces prior chunks; retryable failure preserves the previous version and provider denial invalidates access.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Connection-generation/status trigger deletes sources atomically on disconnect/account switch; connection deletion cascades to sources and composite owner/document FK cascades to chunks. Owner removal is repeat-safe and does not need the processing key. Original-file Google sharing receipts are independent of the removable index; deleting a selection does not revoke an existing Google ACL.
table_families.trust_boundary: Separate server-readable processing domain, not client-key PKM. Source IDs/names, text, provenance and vectors use DRIVE_DOCUMENT_KEY_V1 AES-256-GCM with purpose/owner/document/generation AAD; chunks additionally bind version/ordinal.
