Owner-keyed HMAC source fingerprints support idempotency; no plaintext content hashes, OAuth credentials or vault keys.
table_families.expected_row_growth: Selected-only admission remains bounded to 100 documents; explicitly consented live collection admission grows with accessible files and uses paged discovery and resumable processing.

table_families.primary_access_path: Default-off owner-protected request/review/approval/delivery/removal routes and finite durable worker entrypoints. One OIDC-protected, default-off bounded UAT sweep sequences indexing, suggestions, permission delivery/reconciliation and notification work; it remains unverified until the scheduler and authenticated acceptance are configured.
table_families.retention_policy: Requests have a 30-day authority lifetime and reviews five minutes; those bounds do not themselves delete records. Encrypted management receipts survive ordinary disconnect/index removal. Hard scheduled retention remains a release prerequisite.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Transactional reset/deletion erases private requests, reviews and app-identity linkage. Recipient erasure preserves only another owner's encrypted exact Google-management facts, not request narratives, filenames, source versions, recipient provider subject or full ACL snapshots. Owner erasure removes those receipts; it never claims to revoke external Google sharing.
table_families.trust_boundary: DRIVE_SHARING_KEY_V1 is independent of document/OAuth keys. AES-256-GCM envelopes bind owner, resource and purpose. Google IDs, names, live content fingerprints, verified account identity, purpose, coverage, exact approval, the owner's Allow with its price, and permission receipts remain encrypted; only opaque workflow IDs, statuses, source versions, keyed binding digests and workflow timestamps such as owner_allowed_at and server-proven existing_access_waived_at are plaintext. A confirmation claim and pending work commit atomically before external calls.

table_families.primary_access_path: One USD Stripe Checkout order is created only after an eligible Drive request, from the owner's Trusted circle or explicitly allowed by the owner, has a nonempty frozen shareable batch. New requests lock the owner's effective quote from 50 to 50000 cents at creation; legacy requests retain their original price rule. The authenticated requester alone may open Checkout. A signature-verified Stripe webhook confirms the exact session, amount, currency and requester binding before grant workers may continue. The return URL does not confer payment authority.
table_families.retention_policy: At most one live order and one account-free obligation per request, plus one refund attempt and verified event dedupe receipts. Checkout URLs expire with their Stripe session and are cleared on settlement. The obligation and refund evidence, including an opaque existing_access_waived_at marker bound to a retired unpaid checkout, survive request erasure until payment and refund duties are settled under merchant retention policy. The marker permits full late-money reconciliation without treating free preexisting receipts as purchased delivery.
table_families.deletion_behavior: The live order cascades from the request. Before account reset or erasure removes the request, an opaque obligation snapshots delivery state and removes all account linkage; late signed charges and in-flight refunds remain reconcilable. Stripe's own merchant records follow the payment account's retention policy.
table_families.trust_boundary: The retained obligation has only a random request UUID, payer digest, amount (integer cents, 50 to 50000 cents) and currency, Stripe provider IDs, status and timestamps. No account ID, email, filename, search term, request purpose, document ID, content or Checkout URL is retained there. The requester-visible Feed event is never written after erasure. Orders and retained obligations bind an immutable Stripe mode; unproven legacy rows cannot authorize live money. Current-mode processing never reinterprets a test Checkout or refund as live.

table_families.primary_access_path: An authenticated document owner sets one USD Drive request price in integer cents from 50 to 50000 in Profile. Request creation locks the effective price and version on the encrypted request; later edits affect future requests only.
table_families.retention_policy: One active preference row per owner while the account exists. The default price applies when no custom preference is enabled.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account reset and erasure remove the preference row. Existing payment obligations retain their original quoted amount without the profile setting.
table_families.trust_boundary: Only the authenticated owner may read or change the preference. Server-side quote/version checks bind the requester to the price at request creation.

table_families.primary_access_path: New eligible paid Drive orders enroll one owner earning. Signed charge, refund, delivery and Stripe fee evidence determine a 3% platform share and one idempotent Connect transfer after confirmed delivery.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain unsettled earnings and transfer or reversal evidence through financial reconciliation under the merchant retention policy. Historical orders are not backfilled.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account erasure removes live identity joins but retains the opaque obligation and provider settlement identifiers until any earned share, refund or reversal is resolved.
table_families.trust_boundary: No document name, search term, bank number or user ID is stored in the retained payout row. Stripe account IDs and charge or transfer IDs remain restricted to service-role settlement paths. Settlement binds the original test/live payment mode and verified destination; changing runtime mode cannot convert an old earning into live money.

table_families.primary_access_path: A separately signed connected-account Stripe webhook deduplicates events, verifies current provider state and updates aggregate bank-deposit status. Bank creation, update and deletion events also refresh readiness. Authenticated owners read recent deposits through the current owner-plus-mode connected-account mapping.
table_families.retention_policy: Provider payout and event receipts support settlement, reversal and duplicate-event reconciliation under the merchant retention policy.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Deleting the owner's connected-account mapping removes their app access to these account-keyed financial receipts; any retained provider evidence remains restricted to settlement operators.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores Stripe Connect account and payout IDs, amounts, status, mode, failure code and timestamps; each deposit's write-once masked bank snapshot (bank name and last four only), payout method, bank trace reference and reconciliation status; Connect balance snapshots; and itemised balance transactions with server-side provider IDs (balance-transaction, transfer, destination-payment, charge, external-account and payout IDs) plus the reconciliation cursor. No account or routing number and no document request ID is stored. Provider IDs never leave the server except payout (po_) IDs; acct_, ch_, pi_, py_, tr_, trr_ and txn_ IDs are never returned to clients. A deposit may combine several earnings.

table_families.primary_access_path: Vault Owner review may create a versioned, revocable rule for one verified recipient, one exact request purpose and unchanged contents of named Drive files. Each automatic repeat grant rechecks the active rule, recipient, connection generation, file identity, observed content fingerprint and current provider version.
table_families.retention_policy: Keep an active rule until explicit owner revocation or account deletion; a revoked rule no longer authorizes any queued grant. Connection generation changes prevent reuse after reconnect. Scheduled cleanup of inactive rules remains a release prerequisite.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Owner or recipient account deletion removes the rule. Revocation increments its version and marks it inactive; existing Google ACLs require separate recorded permission removal.
table_families.trust_boundary: The exact file boundary, request purpose and recipient email remain encrypted under DRIVE_SHARING_KEY_V1. Plaintext contains opaque participant IDs, keyed identity binding, connection generation, rule version and active status. An ordinary relationship grants no document authority.

table_families.primary_access_path: Vault Owner independently controls background live Drive preparation and owner-level scalar financial summary visibility. Workers check background authority before reads; authenticated public-profile discovery checks the current financial_summary_enabled choice under the owner graph lock. The scalar policy defaults ON and preserves explicit OFF across reconnect and new periods.
table_families.retention_policy: One current preference per owner, retained across connection generation changes until account deletion. Background and financial summary visibility choices have independent revisions; no document content or provider identifier is stored.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Owner account deletion removes the preference. Preparation OFF stops new background reads; summary OFF hides every financial period without reversing an already explicit file Allow or modifying a sale manifest.
table_families.trust_boundary: Only owner ID, connection generation, independent preparation and scalar summary flags, authored policy version, revisions and update time are stored. The default summary policy fabricates no personal acceptance. Legacy explicit per-period hides migrate to owner OFF. Neither preference authorizes a Viewer grant. PostgreSQL owns the choice; a future Redis cache may project it but cannot authorize publication.

table_families.primary_access_path: A connection sends one question about the owner's Drive through vault-owner routes. It stays pending with no Drive read; no worker reads the question. An opaque drive_query_events row (closed type, ids only) notifies the owner that a question arrived and the asker when it is answered or declined. Only the owner's explicit Allow claims it once and runs the owner's own bounded live chat turn; Deny never reads Drive. The asker can cancel a pending or running question; cancel never reads Drive and stops a running Allow from storing an answer.
table_families.retention_policy: Questions carry a seven-day decision lifetime; that bound does not itself delete the record. One answer is stored per allowed question. Scheduled cleanup remains a release prerequisite.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Owner or requester account deletion removes the question and its answer.
table_families.trust_boundary: DRIVE_SHARING_KEY_V1 AES-256-GCM envelopes bind owner, question id and purpose. The question and answer are encrypted. Requesters receive answer text and file titles only, never the owner-only file ids, dates, canonical reserved file refs or private random downstream idempotency key sealed in the answer. The first Share reserves that key once under the question row lock; retries and owner status reads recover only its committed approval. Plaintext holds opaque participant ids, a keyed question digest, status, revision, a closed failure code and timestamps. No preparation worker reads this table.

table_families.primary_access_path: The owner stages a share from chat with one connected person, or with the Trusted circle members the owner accepted by request or invite (contact-sync, circle-only and imported connections never receive). Only the owner's own tap runs one live Drive search under the owner's authority; the found files (at most eight, no folders) are sealed so a share binds exactly what the owner saw, by reference. The owner's explicit selection then goes through the existing exact-file lane (owner-initiated request, owner-selected review, ledger approval, permission worker). The recipient never reads this table.
table_families.retention_policy: A search stays shareable for one hour. One row per owner search and recipient; the shared row keeps the link to its document share request. Expired unreserved searches can be replaced; reserved selections remain for durable approval recovery and never extend the authority lifetime. Scheduled cleanup of terminal unapproved reservations remains a prerequisite for broader rollout.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Owner or recipient account deletion removes the row.
table_families.trust_boundary: DRIVE_SHARING_KEY_V1 AES-256-GCM envelope bound to owner, row id and purpose holds the owner's words, the found files (names, dates, Drive file ids), and the canonical reserved file references/downstream idempotency key after a Share attempt. Plaintext holds opaque participant ids, a keyed request digest, status, the document share request id and timestamps.

table_families.primary_access_path: PostgreSQL file-level mutation serialization, owner-only removal contexts and a finite metadata-only notification outbox worker. It emits only a closed document_share_* type plus opaque request/event IDs (drive_query_events carries the question-lane types for drive_live_query_requests); web/native derives its fixed local review route and the generic push adapter is called outside the lease transaction. No model/caller-controlled provider endpoint or request/provider URL is forwarded.
table_families.retention_policy: A file claim remains through uncertain outcomes until GET-only reconciliation; never expire a potentially dispatched mutation into an automatic retry. An erased-owner uncertain effect retains only an ownerless keyed-file fence without age-based release, requiring Google management. Stable file-lock HMAC keys/fences must survive rotation. Each notification event has at most three dispatch attempts with crash-safe lease recovery; a settled timestamp means dispatch work ended, never device/user receipt. The default-off OIDC scheduler route has a fixed small batch/deadline; configuring it, token registration and live acceptance remain release prerequisites.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Known terminal operations remove live claims. Account reset/deletion removes outbox/private linkage and contexts; recipient erasure retains owner-only contexts for necessary encrypted removal receipts. Owner erasure detaches uncertain claims from deleted operations, leaving no user ID, recipient, provider file ID or credential. Late results cannot reconstruct erased private data.
table_families.trust_boundary: Only opaque request/operation/event IDs, owner linkage, timestamps and keyed file equality HMACs. No filenames, purpose, emails, provider IDs, credentials or content in queued notification metadata.

table_families.primary_access_path: Single-use owner/generation-bound web Picker selection sessions; never a document-read or sharing grant.
table_families.retention_policy: Ten-minute authorization lifetime; at most one session per owner, replaced at next Picker start and deleted on connection invalidation. Scheduled expiry cleanup must be proven before rollout.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Owner connection deletion cascades; disconnect/account switch deletes in the same transaction. Contains no source identifiers or provider credentials.
table_families.trust_boundary: Only Vault Owner protected routes create/consume sessions. A browser event or isAppAuthorized provider field alone cannot authorize ingestion; authenticated explicit confirmation and current generation are both required.

table_families.primary_access_path: Vault Owner starts, reviews, confirms or cancels an owner/generation/credential-version-bound mobile Google One Picker attempt; the fixed HTTPS callback stages only already-validated candidates before the same catalog admission transaction as web Picker.
table_families.retention_policy: Ten-minute attempt lifetime. Starting a new Picker, cancellation, disconnect, generation/version change and expiry invalidate the linked single-use selection session. Completed rows retain no PKCE proof or staged metadata.
table_families.deletion_behavior: The linked drive_picker_sessions foreign key cascades native-attempt removal. Disconnect/account switch removes the session transactionally; late callbacks and confirmations cannot recreate it.
table_families.trust_boundary: PKCE proof and staged metadata are AES-GCM encrypted using the external connector credential service with owner/attempt/generation/version AAD. The drive.file-only callback token is transient and never stored. Plaintext workflow fields do not include OAuth code, token, Google subject, file ID, or filename.

table_families.primary_access_path: One registry service resolves curated definitions and owner-private definitions. Vault-owner POST /api/connectors/registrations uses an owner-bound retry UUID, graph lock and 32-active-registration limit; registration conveys no tool authority. Owner-aware reads require authenticated user_id; legacy reads see only is_active curated rows. Private Settings UI, custom OAuth and governed ADK invocation remain separate acceptance gates.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain active connector definitions while offered; deactivate rather than delete so historical per-user connections remain explainable.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Curated rows remain operator-managed. Account erasure deletes private rows after credential and OAuth-attempt children. Reset disables private rows and scrubs endpoint, labels and authentication metadata, retaining the opaque registration FK for revoked monotonic connection counters. Disposable PostgreSQL verifies owner isolation and FK ordering; registration ingress remains a separate gate. Rollback disables owner_enabled without deleting credentials or history.
table_families.trust_boundary: Configuration metadata only, never credential values or tool results. Private definitions require is_active=false by database constraint so older readers cannot publish them. owner_enabled is separate owner-scoped availability, not OAuth, tool permission, or execution authority. Private endpoint safety and registration are separate gates; status projections omit raw endpoints and schemas.

table_families.primary_access_path: Per-user connect/disconnect status and encrypted credential envelope for one external MCP connector, via external_connector_credentials_service.py
table_families.retention_policy: Retain the encrypted credential while the connection is active; clear the ciphertext immediately on disconnect and keep only the revoked status row.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Explicit account deletion removes credentials and OAuth attempts, then (after commit, best effort) revokes verified envelope-v2 Google Drive grants at Google; legacy envelopes and API-key connectors are not revoked. Reset scrubs credentials and account labels while retaining revoked monotonic generation/version counters to fence late results. Disconnect clears credential_ciphertext/credential_iv immediately rather than waiting for a bounded window.
table_families.trust_boundary: AES-GCM via EXTERNAL_CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_KEY, separate from google_provider_connections and enterprise_crm_registry. Legacy envelopes retain owner/connector AAD. V2 adds generation/version binding and encrypts verified account identity, client, scopes, expiry, and refresh material; queryable expiry is integrity-checked. Lifecycle generations, refresh leases, capability verification, and bounded revocation outcomes contain no provider secrets. Disconnect scrubs credentials before bounded in-memory revocation; failed revocation is not a promise of background retry.

table_families.primary_access_path: Short-lived PKCE attempt state for an oauth-style external connector's start()/complete() round trip, via external_connector_oauth_service.py
table_families.retention_policy: 10-minute authorization lifetime. Finalization, cancellation, disconnect, and superseding attempts scrub pending secrets. Bounded opportunistic cleanup on connector lifecycle traffic scrubs expired material and deletes expired workflow rows older than 24 hours; this is not a scheduled wall-clock purge guarantee.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Disconnect invalidates all attempts for the owner/connector. Account deletion also removes these workflow rows. Cleanup never revokes provider grants or alters an active connection.
table_families.trust_boundary: V2 PKCE verifier and OIDC nonce are encrypted with owner/connector/attempt AAD. Native callbacks may stage an encrypted verified token envelope additionally bound to connection generation; it cannot execute or activate until the original owner finalizes. No plaintext tokens, provider identity, OAuth codes, client secrets, or Vault Owner tokens are stored.

table_families.primary_access_path: UAT-only HushhTech product linking and allowlisted compatibility metadata routes
table_families.retention_policy: Retain active synthetic links and checked-in synthetic shadow metadata only while the UAT cohort is enabled; revoked links may remain through the bounded QA review window.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Revoke or delete Firebase-linked mapping rows on account or fixture teardown; delete synthetic shadow rows when the checked-in fixture is retired. No production legacy record is copied into this family.
table_families.trust_boundary: Firebase UID is the canonical identity. Legacy UUID is provenance only. Shadow rows contain allowlisted synthetic profile, onboarding, access-state, and report-asset metadata; never email mapping evidence, owner tokens, private-place values, PKM plaintext, connector private keys, or production Supabase data.

table_families.primary_access_path: single-use Hussh Research to HushhTech PKCE launch authorize and exchange
table_families.retention_policy: Codes expire after 60 seconds; retain consumed hashes for a 24-hour replay-investigation window, then compact opportunistically on the next authorization.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete expired and consumed rows after the replay window; cascade user-linked rows on canonical actor deletion.
table_families.trust_boundary: Hashed launch codes, Firebase UID, exact audience/redirect, PKCE challenge, and timestamps only. No bearer tokens, custom tokens, verifiers, private keys, or account lookup evidence persist.

table_families.primary_access_path: append-only synthetic link activation, conflict, relink, recovery, import, and revocation audit
table_families.retention_policy: Retain metadata through UAT QA and incident review; compact only under the approved UAT retention process.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Database enforcement rejects row updates and deletes. Link and actor identifiers are immutable audit provenance without foreign-key cascades, so parent teardown cannot rewrite history; later compaction requires the approved UAT audit-retention process.
table_families.trust_boundary: Mapping identifiers, event type, app binding, fixture hash, and bounded proof-session metadata only. No email or phone mapping, session proof body, tokens, secrets, production data, or decrypted Research information.

table_families.primary_access_path: strict checked-in JSONL synthetic shadow importer dry-run, apply, checkpoint, and deterministic replay
table_families.retention_policy: Retain fixture checksums, counts, checkpoints, and terminal state for UAT reconciliation while the synthetic cohort exists.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete with synthetic fixture teardown after QA evidence no longer depends on the run; no destructive down-migration is required for rollback.
table_families.trust_boundary: Fixture names, hashes, counts, checkpoints, stable error codes, and timestamps only. The importer has no Supabase connection/export mode and never stores production rows or credentials.

table_families.primary_access_path: append-only synthetic importer start, transactional per-record outcome, failure, and completion evidence
table_families.retention_policy: Retain bounded event metadata and fixture hashes through UAT reconciliation and QA evidence review; compact only under the approved UAT audit-retention process.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Database enforcement rejects row updates and deletes. Later compaction requires the approved UAT audit-retention process and is never part of importer replay or rollback.
table_families.trust_boundary: Run identifiers, fixture hashes, phases, outcomes, sequences, timestamps, stable error codes, synthetic record identifiers, record types, record hashes, counts, and tombstone flags only. No fixture payload, production row, identity evidence, credential, or decrypted Research information.

table_families.primary_access_path: developer app registration, token issuance, and MCP/developer API access
table_families.retention_policy: Retain active apps/tokens and audit metadata; revoke or expire inactive tokens.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete/revoke by developer app lifecycle; preserve audit metadata where needed.
table_families.trust_boundary: Developer metadata and token hashes/wrappers only; no user PKM payloads.

table_families.primary_access_path: One Feed route: cross-domain activity list, unread badge, and read-state tracking. Counterpart identity uses audit primary keys, indexed grant IDs, or indexed owner/recipient event candidates with exact source and audience checks; current photos join the identity cache. Closed agent outcomes also project canonical provider proposal/connection/job and Circle relationship transitions (migration269). Migration313 emits a committed owner-only feed_changed hint after every changed Feed row, including read state and deletion; the shared backend listener fans out to authenticated owner streams. Hints contain no row contents and have no replay authority: connect, listener recovery and overflow reset require a snapshot. A future broker may replace NOTIFY behind this same invalidation contract.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while the account exists; presentation-only, not a domain audit authority.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Hard-delete owned Feed with account deletion; derived counterpart links cascade when either the Feed event or counterpart account is deleted. No copied photos.
table_families.trust_boundary: The companion table holds server-only counterpart identity references resolved from viewer-authorized source records. They never enter the browser DTO. Presentation-only fan-out from each domain's own audit/event tables (consent, location, connected systems, and the Drive sharing/question outboxes drive_share_events and drive_query_events, projected as connected_systems rows carrying only the closed type, request id, status word and counterpart label) or from a domain's completion point (Kai, KYC, connections). Never stores ciphertext, vault content, or full domain payloads; only bounded, non-sensitive metadata used to render a feed line. Migration269 additionally consumes reviewed Drive directive settlements and standalone bulk-effect/recipient receipts. Only closed outcomes, opaque review IDs, bounded Circle names and authorized connector catalog display names are presented; dedupe identities remain server-only. Queries, filenames, account labels, mailbox IDs, credentials, provider errors and result payloads are excluded.

table_families.primary_access_path: the owner's own Personal World Model doc behind /api/pwm (cross-device preference sync)
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while the account exists; one row per owner, overwritten in place on update.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Hard-delete on account deletion, an explicit DELETE /api/pwm, or an empty PUT.
table_families.trust_boundary: The owner's own plaintext preference metadata, keyed by and returned only to the verified uid; never another party's data and never vault ciphertext.

table_families.primary_access_path: PCHP RFC-002 subscription grants: owner-issued, subscriber-scoped read access to PWM fields (/api/fabric/grants)
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while the grant is active or for audit; revoked/expired grants compacted per retention policy.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete on account deletion; revoke (fail-closed status) on owner revocation or expiry.
table_families.trust_boundary: Grant metadata only (subscriber, scopes, purpose, price, handle fingerprint); never the PWM values and never the plaintext handle.

table_families.primary_access_path: PCHP RFC-002 hash-chained receipt ledger for grant/read/revoke events (/api/fabric/receipts)
table_families.retention_policy: Long-retention append-only audit chain; redact payload detail rather than deleting chain rows.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account export may include safe receipt metadata; deletion redacts user linkage only if legally required, preserving chain integrity. Current state: full account deletion retains these rows with the raw user_id (declared in hushh_mcp/services/account_erasure_policy.py); changing that is a legal policy decision.
table_families.trust_boundary: Signed, hash-chained receipt metadata only (hashes, signatures, scope + field-path labels); no PWM values.

table_families.primary_access_path: tamper-evident hash-chained mirror of the primary consent_audit ledger (NIST 800-53 AU-9/AU-10); written fail-safe behind CONSENT_AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED, verified via ConsentAuditChainService.verify_chain
table_families.retention_policy: Long-retention append-only audit chain; redact payload detail rather than deleting chain rows.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account export may include safe receipt metadata; deletion redacts user linkage only if legally required, preserving chain integrity.
table_families.trust_boundary: Signed, hash-chained consent-event metadata only (hashes, signatures, scope/agent/request labels); never token secrets or PKM values.

table_families.primary_access_path: brand-initiated PCHP RFC-002 pairing requests: create, code lookup, approve/deny, single handle claim (/api/fabric/requests)
table_families.retention_policy: Short-lived pairing workflow: requests expire in minutes; terminal rows compacted per retention policy.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete on account deletion for bound rows; expired/denied/claimed rows are terminal and compactable.
table_families.trust_boundary: Workflow state and grant metadata only; the signed handle is held solely between approval and its single claim, then cleared. Never PWM values; uid binds only at approval from the verified token.

table_families.primary_access_path: GET/POST /api/account/legal-acceptance (Firebase-authenticated, not vault-gated). The web and native app records acceptance of the served Terms of Use and Privacy Policy versions silently at each successful sign-in (the sign-in screen links both documents); there is no in-app re-acceptance prompt. Reads return the latest acceptance of each document.
table_families.retention_policy: Append-only history: one row per person, document, version and effective date. Re-accepting a recorded version keeps the original accepted_at. Kept across account reset.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete rows where the deleting account is user_id on full account deletion (explicit DELETE; no foreign key, because acceptance precedes the actor profile).
table_families.trust_boundary: Document id, version and effective-date labels, surface (web or native) and a server timestamp, keyed by the Firebase UID from the verified token. Carries no user information and grants no access.
table_families.expected_row_growth: two rows per person per legal document version they accept

table_families.primary_access_path: POST /api/one/first-connect-insights claims one row per connected source before generating the picked-up card; the feed attention sweep claims one row per notable feed_events id and counts sent rows for the daily push cap; agent-chat admission of a feedAttention turn reads the sent row.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain while the account exists; one row per (person, kind, subject). Feed attention rows are pruned after 30 days by the sweep.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cascade-delete with the actor profile on account deletion and reset.
table_families.trust_boundary: Kind, subject identifier (a source name or a feed_events id), outcome word and timestamps only. Never inference text, feed item words or One's message: the card lives on the owner's screen and Keep saves through the encrypted PKM writer; One's message is sealed with the owner's chat key.
table_families.expected_row_growth: at most three card rows per person plus one row per notable feed event

table_families.primary_access_path: model preference service, read on every agent chat turn and written from Agent chat or /api/one/models/preference
table_families.retention_policy: Retain one row per person while the account exists; absent row means the deployment default.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cascade-delete with the actor profile on account deletion.
table_families.trust_boundary: Model identifier only, validated against the server-side catalog on write; carries no user information and grants no access.
table_families.expected_row_growth: one row per person who chooses a model

table_families.primary_access_path: Existing owner-scoped private-agent registry, provisioning, key attachment, upgrade and erasure services; dev-only migrations900-947 and PERSONAL_AGENT_ENABLED. Dev-only migration948 adds owner Azure coordinates (tenant, subscription, resource group; location in user_cloud_region), written only by the Connect Azure setup job's job-locked publication, and retires the anypoint placement. Dev-only migration949 retains, once per reserved erasure attempt and before any access is revoked, the pod's crypto-erase confirmation for a user_azure agent with its setup nonce (the agentCryptoErase checkpoint a cut-short revocation resumes from), then the owner-access erasure receipt (that confirmation, the role assignments revoked, the person's remaining resource ids, the vault purge date and the resource group to delete), both validated against the reserved snapshot; account deletion still refuses while those resources remain. Dev-only migration950 adds placement_epoch (0 for every existing row, bumped by one on every standby promotion); the hub verifier refuses a signed pod request whose X-Hushh-Pod-Epoch is missing or stale once the person has a standby or an epoch above 0
table_families.retention_policy: Retain exact provisioning, update, removal and erasure attempts until resource reconciliation settles. The existing executor consumes deletion intents; unresolved absence or provider retention remains explicit, never inferred from elapsed time.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Suspend new work before approved cleanup. Preserve exact resource/custody evidence and attempt identity through retry; finalize only when provider absence or the declared retained-resource outcome is verified. Cloud-only removal preserves the account; full account erasure has its own generation-bound authority.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores opaque owner/HusshID bindings, keyed phone hashes, public keys, provider coordinates and bounded lifecycle evidence. Azure coordinates are directory, subscription and resource-group identifiers only; one owner per resource group is enforced by a partial unique index. No raw phone, private key, OAuth token or provider payload belongs in registry metadata. Owner locks and exact-attempt publication govern provisioning; PKM and agent memory remain separate authorities. Dev-only migration947 adds the pod's public request-signing key and key id (recorded only from a hub-initiated pull, bound to pod_pubkey) and the one-way identity_mode latch; they are removed with the row by the same deletion path.
table_families.expected_row_growth: one registry row per owner; bounded nested attempt/evidence objects, plus deliberately retained deletion intents

table_families.primary_access_path: Dev-only migration947. The hub's signed pod-request verifier (hushh_mcp/services/pod_request_verifier.py via pod_request_identity_store.py) consumes one (kid, nonce) per verified request with INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; a conflicting insert is a replay and is refused. Reached only where pod_hub_identity_auth_enabled is on.
table_families.retention_policy: Rows live only for the signature acceptance window plus a skew margin (about 120 seconds after the signing time); expired rows are pruned opportunistically by the verifier at most once a minute per process.
table_families.deletion_behavior: No owner column and no per-account rows: account deletion needs no action. A row names only a public-key-derived kid and a random nonce, cannot be joined to a person once the registry row is deleted, and self-expires within about two minutes.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores a public-key-derived key id, a random 16-byte nonce and an expiry timestamp. No user identifiers, personal information, tokens, request bodies or signatures; a row grants no access and only prevents replay.

table_families.primary_access_path: Dev-only migration950. hushh_mcp/services/personal_agent_standby_store.py (statements in personal_agent_standby_sql.py): add_standby for a provisioned, signing primary (latching identity_mode), read_standby for the hub signed-request verifier's key and epoch fence, claim_sync_lease / list_standbys_due / record_sync_result for the standby sync, swap_primary_and_standby for a switch (one statement, fenced on placement_epoch and the observed standby pod_key_id, promoting only a standby with a completed sync), remove_standby keeping coordinates only under the registry's backend_metadata.detachedPlacements. Design: docs/future/personal-agent/STANDBY-SYNC.md.
table_families.retention_policy: One row per person while that person keeps a standby agent; removed by remove_standby (coordinates, never keys, retained under the registry row's detachedPlacements) or with the account.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account deletion refuses while a standby row exists, exactly as it refuses the primary's external resources, at the same point under the same owner locks (including after a finished primary erasure; hushh_mcp/services/personal_agent_standby_guard.py). The account path issues no standby delete: the row references its registry row ON DELETE RESTRICT, so a row that ever survived the guard would make the registry delete fail and roll the whole erasure back.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores the standby's placement coordinates (target, host id, cloud project or directory, subscription and resource group), its https address, its public pod and request-signing keys with their ids, and sync progress (last synced sequence, 64-hex chain head, timestamps, an advisory lease id). No private key, token, bundle, record or content: the hub ferries ciphertext it cannot open. The standby's keys and host must differ from the primary's (deferred constraint trigger), so the verifier can always tell the two placements apart.
table_families.expected_row_growth: at most one row per person who adds a standby agent

table_families.primary_access_path: agent prompt-sync read path (GET /api/one/agent-prompt), flag-off
table_families.retention_policy: Retain active and superseded system-prompt versions for rollback and audit; no per-user rows.
table_families.deletion_behavior: No per-user deletion; system-prompt configuration is pruned only by admin policy.
table_families.trust_boundary: System-prompt configuration and version hashes only; contains no personal data.

table_families.primary_access_path: server-side WebAuthn/FIDO2 registration and authentication ceremony (flag-off, WEBAUTHN_ENABLED; migration parked)
table_families.retention_policy: Retain a user's registered authenticators while the account exists.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Hard-delete with account deletion; a user may remove an individual authenticator.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores the credential id, COSE public key, and sign count only; a public key is not a secret and no private key material is ever held.

table_families.primary_access_path: transient WebAuthn challenge issue/consume during a registration or authentication ceremony (flag-off; migration parked)
table_families.retention_policy: Short-lived security nonces: challenges expire in minutes (5-minute TTL) and are single-use.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Deleted on consume (before validation, so a challenge can never be replayed) or on expiry; user_id may be null for usernameless auth.
table_families.trust_boundary: Ephemeral ceremony state (a random challenge, RP id, ceremony kind) only; no personal data or credential material.

table_families.primary_access_path: message feedback service, written from the Agent One chat thumbs control via /api/one/agent-chat/feedback and read for response-quality reporting
table_families.retention_policy: Retain one row per rated assistant turn while the conversation exists.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cascade-delete with the ADK session on conversation deletion and with the actor profile on account deletion; clearing a rating deletes the row.
table_families.trust_boundary: Rating and message reference only; never message content, prompt or model output, so no vault key and no decrypt path are involved.
table_families.expected_row_growth: at most one row per assistant turn a person chooses to rate

table_families.primary_access_path: OneLocationAccountSettingsService (owner-level sharing on/off, precision preference, reported OS permission; migration 221) and OneLocationSetupService (voice-first Location setup step machine; migration 223) behind GET/PATCH /api/one/location/account-settings and /setup-progress (vault-owner token) and the One Live Voice tools. Turning sharing off revokes active share grants and public links in the same transaction; Location write paths enforce the posture.
table_families.retention_policy: One mutable row per user for as long as the account exists.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Hard-delete with account deletion (FK ON DELETE CASCADE to actor_profiles).
table_families.trust_boundary: Coordinate-free by construction: only posture enums, consent version/timestamps, precision preference, and reported OS permission state. Precision is a preference; coarsening happens on the device before recipient encryption.

table_families.primary_access_path: hushh_mcp/one_voice ConversationStore and PendingActionStore used by the One Live Voice relay (WS /api/one/voice/live) and the pending-action HTTP twins (migration 222). Conversations hold the canonical-id entity context, the provider resumption handle, and per-session counters; pending actions are confirmation-gated voice mutations (voice or tap tier, hashed single-use receipt, one open per conversation, 120 s TTL).
table_families.retention_policy: Conversations expire two hours after last activity; pending actions expire after their TTL and are marked expired on read. Both are operational ledgers, not history.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Hard-delete with account deletion (FK ON DELETE CASCADE to actor_profiles); pending actions cascade from their conversation.
table_families.trust_boundary: No audio, transcripts, coordinates, tokens, or spoken names are stored. Entity context holds canonical ids plus display names the server itself returned; receipts are stored as SHA-256 hashes; tool args are canonical ids only.

table_families.primary_access_path: Owner-confirmed search create/status/results/stop; existing Drive worker claims bounded metadata-only page slices. Owner+client idempotency, one active job per owner, keyed result deduplication and lease CAS. No document indexing or sharing authority. Period preparations also retain owner-only original results and separate advisory classifier tags in sealed metadata; neither grants buyer access.
table_families.retention_policy: Ordinary jobs/results retain the 24-hour TTL. Period packets pin only the current source job and retained prior-preview job while replacement has no usable results; each has at most 10000 result rows. Bounded 100-job cleanup removes expired unreferenced period revisions and rotates a housekeeping-only inspection time for pinned rows so later history is not starved.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account erasure deletes owner jobs; result rows cascade. Stop invalidates the lease. Ordinary expired jobs and unreferenced expired period ciphertext are deleted; pinned current/previous owner results remain until replaced or their packet/account is erased.
table_families.trust_boundary: Explicit job-scoped metadata-search consent plus current verified live grant/generation. Existing DriveSharingCipher uses DRIVE_SHARING_KEY_V1 and owner/resource/purpose-bound AES-GCM. Query, provider cursors, shared-drive IDs and result metadata encrypted; no document content or owner session tokens persisted.
table_families.expected_row_growth: At most 10,000 results per job; ordinary 24-hour TTL; at most two pinned discovery jobs per period head plus bounded transient superseded history.

table_families.primary_access_path: Vault-owner preview and approval of a frozen Drive search; bounded workers create and reconcile Google permissions for exact files, then remove app-created direct permissions after the owner confirms Stop access. Recipients see only confirmed grants through their authenticated Shared with you collection.
table_families.retention_policy: An unapproved review has a 24-hour authority lifetime. Approval and progress extend workflow access for seven days independently of the source search. The timestamps fence reads and worker claims; scheduled physical purging of expired bulk-share rows remains required.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Owner erasure removes the share, frozen files, recipients, effects, notifications, and pending removal plans. Recipient erasure pseudonymizes its app ID in owner-held removal plans so recorded Google access can still be managed. Deletion of local records alone does not revoke Google permissions; confirmed Stop queues verified provider removal first.
table_families.trust_boundary: Owner approval binds the frozen encrypted file manifest, verified recipient identities, revision and review digest. File metadata, recipient identities, successful permission receipts, and removal plans are sealed under DRIVE_SHARING_KEY_V1. Plaintext contains opaque workflow references, bounded counts, leases, states and timestamps. Grant workers recheck payment and current authority; Stop fences new grants. Removal workers delete only permissions with app-created receipts under the original Google issuer, verify absence, and never blindly repeat an uncertain DELETE. Recipient links are exposed only after confirmed grants and hidden on Stop.

table_families.primary_access_path: Authenticated Circle chat service: membership-scoped keyset reads, ciphertext/image writes, member key envelopes, unread acknowledgements, mute preferences and durable generic push leases. Sender-only encrypted edits and global tombstones retain original envelopes; bounded metadata reconciliation and independently authorized reply resolution repair loaded history.
table_families.retention_policy: Messages retained for the lifetime of the ordinary Circle; client images bounded to 5 MB, text to 4000 characters, pages to 50 and rendered windows to 300. No automatic expiry of conversation history. Pushes stop after five attempts.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Circle soft/hard deletion erases messages, images, envelopes and preferences and removes associated Feed rows. Reset/full account erasure deletes authored messages and recipient-owned envelopes/preferences. Actor-profile cascades provide an additional deletion boundary. Leave/rejoin suppresses old pushes and Feed unread rows; prior-generation envelopes remain inaccessible. Message actions retain original recipient epochs; viewer deletion hides only that copy; sender deletion replaces content with a client-encrypted tombstone, clears encrypted attachments and previews, suppresses pushes and removes Feed projections. Deleted content is never restored by rollback.
table_families.trust_boundary: Active ordinary Circle members only, with an envelope matching the current membership joined_at generation. The server relays client ciphertext and recipient public keys; it never receives message or image plaintext. Reply UUID references and monotonic revisions are metadata, not history access grants. Replies are independently authorized for each recipient; edits never reseal old content for the current roster.

table_families.primary_access_path: hushh_mcp/services/scope_commerce owns PostgreSQL tariffs, immutable quotes, a shared funded-balance journal, reservations, pending earnings, original-source refunds and Connect settlement. api/routes/scope_commerce.py resolves existing authenticated request/owner authority; consent/paid_admission.py gates canonical exports independently of admission flags. Replaceable Stripe adapters persist provider operations before I/O and reconcile outside financial transactions.
table_families.retention_policy: Financial journal and opaque obligations remain append-only under the approved financial retention policy, including after account erasure. Temporary encrypted staging is cleared on term completion, failure, revocation and erasure; provider retention deadlines govern small residual balances. Live enablement remains gated on verified business configuration, retention, country and tax approvals; source inspection alone does not establish deployed reconciliation or retention behavior.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Revoke affected purchases and block retrieval immediately, release or refund liabilities through original funding provenance, then detach human identity mappings while preserving opaque money obligations and provider settlement routing. Financial reconciliation must continue after erasure and feature rollback; ciphertext deletion cannot withdraw copies already delivered.
table_families.trust_boundary: Integer money and balanced append-only entries use PostgreSQL transactions and reservations; caller receipts and Checkout redirects are not payment evidence. Owner-approved immutable quotes bind exact scope, duration, app and recipient key, with separate human payer confirmation. Only a future fixed-time owner-encrypted export activates paid access; payment never broadens consent or refresh. Stripe receives opaque financial references, never decrypted information, private keys or request purpose.

table_families.primary_access_path: Authenticated Circle chat member reactions and membership event history, rendered as reaction counts and system pills for current members. A nullable event batch UUID groups only one reviewed multi-person add; it grants no access.
table_families.retention_policy: Reaction choices remain while their message and reacting member exist. Membership events remain while their Circle exists and are shown only from the viewer's current membership generation.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Message, Circle and account deletion cascade reaction rows; leaving or removal clears that member's reactions. Circle deletion erases event history, and actor deletion nulls event actor and subject identifiers.
table_families.trust_boundary: Only active Circle members can react or read event history. Plaintext contains exact sequences from the Unicode Emoji 17.0 reaction catalogue (maximum 16 code points), event kind, opaque actor, subject and optional batch identifiers, and timestamps; encrypted message content and keys never enter these tables or notifications.

table_families.primary_access_path: Transactional direct-message outbox and shared Circle/direct device delivery workers; source eligibility is rechecked before FCM acceptance.
table_families.retention_policy: Message history keeps its existing policy. Push sources expire after one day or five attempts; delivery records deduplicate retries for the source lifetime.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Source deletion cascades to its outbox and delivery records. Account erasure cascades recipient-owned records; tombstones suppress further sends. Installation unregister removes preview keys and token registrations.
table_families.utilization_policy: Delivery metadata is used only for eligible recipient alerts and retry deduplication.
table_families.trust_boundary: Verified recipient, active connection/current Circle membership, block/mute/read/deletion checks, installation owner/key lifecycle fences. No plaintext message or avatar persists in these tables.

table_families.primary_access_path: Owner-confirmed canonical Wallet commits register saved payment cards automatically, including older cards refreshed by the owner's Share action. Owner grants bind individual active connections; authenticated recipients read only their current grant. The same policy orchestrates selected Profile fields through a separate source adapter; outgoing and received participant history is paginated independently of live card eligibility.
table_families.retention_policy: Reservations have a 24-hour original Add window; a later confirmed owner Wallet write can register them as saved cards. Removed registrations remain terminal. Grants authorize reads for exactly 5, 10 or 15 minutes. Expiry ends access, not storage. Registration, idempotency and audit history remain until account erasure; no scheduled history purge is claimed.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Card or Wallet-domain removal marks provenance removed and revokes grants. Account erasure removes owner and recipient grants and dependent request/audit records through the account deletion table map and foreign keys. Historical message references contain no card credentials.
table_families.trust_boundary: Server-only provenance and recipient binding. Approved masked fields are encrypted with owner/card or owner/recipient/grant purpose binding. PAN, cardholder name, CVV, PIN and vault keys never enter these tables. Postgres enforces expiry/revocation; ordinary connections require fresh same-user verification. Explicit owner-added Trusted Circle membership alone exempts additional verification. Profile values use the existing canonical public projection live, intersected with fields permitted when shared; no additional profile values are stored in grants or history. Profile pause gates reads; source revocation and deletion permanently revoke its grants.

table_families.primary_access_path: Paid answers on a connected person's profile: any active connection submits a question through Request scope; the required semantic resolver stage proposes scopes, deterministic fail-closed validation drops anything the owner does not hold or that another person may never request, and the owner approves the exact question, the exact scopes and a whole-dollar price. The approved terms are fixed by a terms_digest covering question, scopes, both participants and the quote.
table_families.retention_policy: Retained while the request is open and for bounded consent-audit review after it is answered, declined, cancelled or expired; default expiry 30 days from creation.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete every row for either participant on account reset and account deletion; scopes cascade with the request.
table_families.trust_boundary: Holds the requester's own question text and scope references only. No PKM value, no answer content, and no vault or key material. A scope absent from the approved set was never paid for and must never reach an answer.

table_families.primary_access_path: Sibling of drive_request_payment_authority for the question lane. A USD Stripe Checkout order opens only after a completed nonempty staged envelope and owner approval of a question at a whole-dollar price from 100 to 50000 cents. The signed Stripe webhook, routed on payment_kind 'pkm_answer', settles only when the session, attempt, amount, currency and terms_digest all match the locked order; a per-lane event table makes a replayed event a no-op. Refunds cover owner decline, requester cancellation, fulfilment timeout and an empty answer.
table_families.retention_policy: Retained while payment or refund is unsettled and for bounded financial and consent-audit review afterwards; the obligation mirror is identity-free and survives erasure so a late charge can still settle.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Orders delete with the request on account reset and deletion; the identity-free obligation row is retained to reconcile an outstanding charge or refund.
table_families.trust_boundary: Stores amounts, Stripe references and the terms digest. No question text, no answer content, no card data: the card is handled entirely by Stripe Checkout. The obligation mirror carries a salted request/payer hash instead of a user id.

table_families.primary_access_path: The unlocked owner device retrieves exact approved scope slices from the shared encrypted source-linked memory.md, refreshing stale/missing slices from authoritative PKM/account facts before absence. Every successful answer is composed by consent-gated Gemini with approved values and freshness metadata only, then sealed to the requester ECDH P-256 key. New staging requires a request-bound composition receipt; requester access is released only after verified settlement. Historical immutable staged orders retain recovery and settlement eligibility.
table_families.retention_policy: Retained while the requester may still read the delivered answer; removed with the request.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Hard-delete with the request on account reset and account deletion for either participant.
table_families.trust_boundary: Delivery persistence contains ciphertext, source revision numbers and reserved signed composition/terms metadata with keyed input/answer digests; the backend has no answer-decryption key. Approved plaintext transits the separately consented transient Gemini call with NO_CONTENT application telemetry. The receipt proves successful composition for approved terms, not plaintext equality inside client ciphertext. No vault key or general decryption authority is transferred. Reserved receipt metadata is excluded from requester DTOs.

table_families.primary_access_path: Durable settlement for the paid-answer lane, on its separately authenticated answer work drain, using each obligation's stored Stripe mode. A refund obligation is written in the same transaction as the decline, cancellation, empty answer or deadline expiry that caused it, then claimed under a lease and retried on its own backoff with a stable per-request idempotency key. An owner earning becomes due only when an answer is delivered with content, pays gross minus 300 bps commission to the owner's Stripe Connect account, and is voided if the order is refunded.
table_families.retention_policy: Retained while a refund or transfer is unsettled and for bounded financial review afterwards; terminal rows stay as settlement evidence.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Keyed to pkm_answer_payment_obligations rather than the order, so a refund or transfer can still reconcile after the request and both accounts are erased.
table_families.trust_boundary: Amounts, Stripe references and a closed safe_error_code set only. No provider message is copied into the database, and no user id, question text or answer content is stored.

table_families.primary_access_path: Profile Payouts reads owner-scoped live and sandbox wallets. Verified document settlement appends one immutable net-cent credit per request; each live earning also seeds an isolated test demonstration balance. Test redemption reserves coins under a wallet row lock, then reconciles an idempotent Stripe test transfer before appending a debit. Postgres is authoritative; future Redis may cache projections only and never authorize spending.
table_families.retention_policy: Financial entries and redemption obligations retained for reconciliation and audit. One wallet per owner and Stripe mode; append-only entries keyed uniquely to source obligations. Live redemption is unavailable until separately enabled by a reviewed production release.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Actor profile erasure detaches owner identity and holds the wallet; ownerless financial entries and unknown provider obligations survive. Never cascade-delete money or convert legacy transfers into credits.
table_families.trust_boundary: Server-only wallet ownership, mode, integer amounts, opaque request and provider references. No bank details, card data, or document content. One Hashcoin equals one USD cent. Test redemption can never debit live earnings; original order settlement method is immutable.

table_families.primary_access_path: Explicit owner background and processing consent permits resumable Changes API discovery, original-document extraction/OCR, semantic facts and canonical packet preparation. Separately admitted period packets use owner-scoped provider metadata discovery and encrypted query provenance; they do not enable continuous collection or imply content assessment. Owner-authenticated routes manage preparation and listing. A separate vault-owner scalar receipt read permits public-summary withdrawal even when OAuth or background processing is off. Authenticated public-profile viewers, including non-connections, receive only scalar financial summaries allowed by the default-ON owner visibility preference; private purchase routes retain current connection and approval checks. Worker writes use generation, source-version and lease fences. Financial preparations use a versioned predefined query and independently organize saved candidates with the unchanged local bounded-head classifier, without enabling whole-Drive indexing. Migration 429 adds only the head sale_finalization_revision scalar: the existing owner/generation-fenced packet worker may attempt an empty-sale finalization once per saved discovery revision, preserving prior immutable versions and request pins.
table_families.retention_policy: Current collection cursors and workflow state are replaced as progress commits. Versioned extraction, facts and packet evidence are retained while their parent records exist; background pause stops processing without deleting evidence. Historical packet manifests preserve exact approval and purchase evidence. A time-based purge of superseded evidence is not implemented.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Connection generation invalidation removes connected documents; their extraction, page and fact children cascade. Packet availability is fenced by active connection, consent, generation, source versions and freshness. Connection deletion cascades packet heads and versions. Account reset and deletion explicitly remove owner packet heads and cascade their encrypted versions, sources and listings; reset retains only the connector generation fence. Account deletion removes remaining owner-bound state; request packet foreign keys become null while independently encrypted approved request and financial records retain their established lifecycle.
table_families.trust_boundary: Source identifiers, filenames, page text, document facts, citations, packet membership, assessments and provider checkpoints remain owner/resource/purpose-bound encrypted evidence. Plaintext contains opaque IDs, versions, keyed digests, work statuses, timestamps, bounded pricing, explicit listing policy and authored period-packet category/date/timezone selectors. Provider-discovery packets do not assert content facts or citations. Preparation consent never authorizes publication or buyer access. Public scalar count, completeness, freshness and price projections use the distinct drive-financial-summary-default-v1 product policy and canonical owner flag in drive_live_preferences. A saved OFF suppresses all periods, including new versions, while public reads retain current profile and source-generation gates. The policy is independent from preparation and connection-only listing consent, fabricates no personal acceptance, and never authorizes private file access. Saved discovery counts and exact immutable sale membership remain separate projections; legacy per-period publication receipts retain their historical meaning only. Provider/model I/O occurs outside database transactions. Candidate tags are advisory; the server-managed processing policy records no fabricated personal acceptance. Explicit background Off and placement refusal remain enforced. The sale_finalization_revision receipt contains no source metadata or private contents, grants no buyer access or listing authority, and follows its existing head retention and deletion contract.
table_families.expected_row_growth: Proportional to consented accessible files, pages and source versions; canonical membership avoids every possible file combination. Superseded-version storage requires operational growth monitoring.

table_families.primary_access_path: Authenticated PWM invitation create/list/revoke/claim routes. Shared account graph locks and existing transaction connection for strict owner authority.
table_families.retention_policy: Seven-day expiry; expired rows are removed on invitation creation. Rejection/revocation deletes; claim clears transferable ciphertext.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Delete either participant rows on account reset; actor_profiles cascading foreign keys delete on account erasure. Migration refreshes canonical deleted-identity guards.
table_families.trust_boundary: Contact commitment and token hash remain metadata. Public professional preview is encrypted with a token-derived key; the token and plaintext are never stored. Recipient verified-contact claim transfers selected preview to their vault and may start research only with explicit recipient consent. No inviter access to full PWM.

table_families.primary_access_path: Transactional trigger on operator-owned OAuth connection row changes and owner-token GET /api/one/source-journal/connectors. Events are change hints; the owner client rereads the curated connector overview before encrypted projection.
table_families.retention_policy: At most 2048 committed events per owner, pruned in the append transaction. The retained floor and head survive pruning so older cursors receive resetRequired and require an authoritative snapshot. There is no time-based purge while the owner remains active.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Account reset erases owner event rows and upserts the retained hash/sequence watermark, even without prior journal state, so every older cursor requires a new authoritative snapshot without sequence reuse. Full erasure deletes both journal tables for the owner after connector cleanup in the same transaction. Root-delete triggers cover rolling older runtimes, and full-erasure tombstones suppress later source append. Ordinary connector-row deletion appends a deleted hint.
table_families.trust_boundary: Only one-way SHA-256 owner commitment, operator connector ID, event UUID, commit-ordered sequence, changed/deleted operation, schema version, and time. table_families.trust_boundary: Only a one-way owner commitment, source kind, operation, event UUID, sequence, version and time are stored. No source values, row IDs, counterpart identity, payment IDs, documents, location, credentials or vault keys. Hints grant no access.

table_families.trust_boundary: Stores internal owner UID, opaque grant ID, monotonic generation, one checked-in active curated OAuth provider ID and source kind, review contract version and timestamps only. table_families.trust_boundary: Stores internal owner UID, selected provider ID, grant and revision metadata, AAD and ciphertext hashes, and owner AES-GCM nonce/ciphertext. No canonical vault key, pilot DEK, wrapped key, owner token, plaintext connector status, OAuth credential, attestation assertion, worker lease or checkpoint. table_families.trust_boundary: Flags, UUIDs, closed outcomes and delivery timestamps only. No names, contacts, findings, queries, plaintext keys or tokens.

table_families.trust_boundary: Authenticated same-user vault owner, participant-bound reads, active unblocked connections and target-only response. Recipient and card selection remain server-bound; no PAN, CVV, PIN, vault keys, card inventory or card values are stored in requests. Request metadata remains outside Live Memory.

table_families.primary_access_path: Public browser-bound OTP request/verify and authenticated hushh-mail-api delivery worker. Firebase remains identity authority.

table_families.trust_boundary: Current exact-domain policy, keyed single-use verifier, browser binding, durable budgets and fresh verified Firebase primary-email checks under UID finalization authority. No WorkOS dependency or consent/vault authority.

table_families.primary_access_path: Source-transaction triggers enqueue SMS/Location shares, location requests, Circle membership and connection requests; leased background worker reads current sources and installation ownership before provider acceptance. table_families.trust_boundary: Current source status and exact request/membership epoch, recipient registry locks and account lifecycle barriers. No coordinates, encrypted envelope, private message, provider token or rendered notification text is stored.

table_families.primary_access_path: Firebase-authenticated GET/PUT /api/one/models/private-text-approval records an owner's explicit UAT Azure text-processing choice; document request admission and each model call verify the current generation.

table_families.primary_access_path: Production pilot or explicitly expanded registered-contact observer, signed PLG v2 metadata projection, and separately keyed private paginated registered-account audience. Migration 367 adds domain-authored Calendar/explicit-consent/direct-Location value receipts and a canonical information-request/Mail-send association; per-agent signed outcome adapters read retained domain evidence.
table_families.retention_policy: Observation reads enforce a seven-day expiry; existing authenticated Drive work drain purges at most 1000 expired rows per pass. At most 500 observations per owner per UTC day, with explicit limited/best-effort coverage. Epochs remain while the account exists and rotate on reset. Value receipts share the seven-day TTL and reset epoch, with a separate 500-per-owner/day cap and the same bounded purge pass.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cascade with actor identity; full delete explicitly removes observations and epochs. Reset rotates the epoch under the existing writer barrier and clears observations, fencing delayed callbacks. Value receipts are explicitly cleared on reset and delete and cascade with the observation epoch; delayed callbacks retain their captured generation.
table_families.trust_boundary: No authorization, reward, content or task settlement authority. Owner-bound admitted callbacks or authenticated Firebase reports, production lane and explicit pilot UID allowlist or default-off expanded registered-contact admission. Anonymous UID presence alone never admits expanded collection. The independently keyed audience read joins current canonical identity under lifecycle/phone/row barriers without enrollment, identity mutation, messaging consent or delivery. Missing terminals mean possible incomplete observations, not confirmed abandonment. No prompts, arguments, responses, private tool names, provider IDs, routes, coordinates or financial details. RLS denies browser roles. Value receipts are metadata projections after provider acknowledgement or a verified explicit owner decision, never new action authority. They retain no provider IDs, private content, or tokens. Other adapters read domain-owned canonical records; internal stages are not activation journeys.

table_families.primary_access_path: Firebase-owner-bound optional setup/account email preference. A separately signed production-only integration reads at most 25 coalesced pending revisions and acknowledges exact revisions. Generation-fenced revocation cannot subscribe; fresh permission/address checks precede sending. One settings write and its pending projection commit atomically.
table_families.retention_policy: One current preference and one coalesced change row per account. Preferences persist until full account deletion, independently of product reset. Acknowledged active rows may be reconciled hourly; hash-only erasure rows retain suppression without raw identity. No append-only recipient or content history is introduced.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Migration-201 account lifecycle barriers guard reads/writes. Full deletion removes the preference and records an atomic hash-only pending erasure; the tombstone trigger also covers rolling older application deletions. Product reset preserves explicit permission and opt-out. Delayed acknowledgements cannot clear newer revisions.
table_families.trust_boundary: Identity, Terms, research notices, writing style, usage and vault authorization do not establish marketing permission. Initial positive choice requires the current Firebase verified email and binds its hash. No default enrollment, phone/SMS permission, alias substitution, task-completion claim or action authority. Browser roles cannot read operational tables. UI mutations are manual-only and excluded from agent execution. These settings remain outside Live Memory and shareable attr scopes.

table_families.primary_access_path: Default-off, cohort-admitted Vault Owner routes expose state, fiscal folders and bounded category file pages, accept explicit preparation opt-in, and erase entries. The retained Google Drive connector presents Data packets below Trusted documents. The independent groups DriveWorkDrain stage uses current live grants, owner placement and generation/revision-fenced renewable leases; a run is bounded to 180 seconds, one owner by default, at most 200 entries and 20 uploaded-content reads. Its fixed UAT scheduler requires explicit feature activation. No direct client database access.
table_families.retention_policy: Retain the derived sealed index while the connection generation exists, until owner erase or connection revocation/change. Pausing retains entries. No age-based TTL or scheduled retention is implemented. A complete uncapped inventory prunes absent files; partial or capped inventories never prune. Organizer placements are refreshable from Drive, but owner overrides are not reconstructible from the provider and are preserved by behavioral rollback. This server projection is not canonical PKM memory.

The migration trigger deletes both tables' rows on connection-generation change or revocation; connector deletion cascades to both tables. Account reset uses that generation/revocation path and account deletion removes the connector. Migration 410 refreshes account-deletion write guards. These are source contracts, not deployed account-erasure evidence.
table_families.trust_boundary: Separate server-key processing domain under DRIVE_DOCUMENT_KEY_V1, not client-key BYOK or zero knowledge. Drive file IDs, names, links and retained text starts/vectors are AES-256-GCM sealed with purpose, owner, source reference and connection generation as associated data. Source references are owner-keyed HMACs. Shelf/candidate/confidence/reason/model and provider revisions, deciding dates, counts, opt-in, time zone and lease state remain queryable personal metadata. Only kept entries retain text starts/vectors. Placements confer no sharing, consent, search or provider-write authority; explicit opt-in, live grant, cohort, background preference and lease revisions remain authoritative.
table_families.expected_row_growth: One state row and at most 10000 indexed entries per owner; batches up to 200 entries, including at most 20 uploaded-content reads, with a 204800 raw-byte prefix cap per file. Inventory traversal is bounded to 400 provider pages. No age compaction. Partial refresh state is persisted; only a complete uncapped listing permits pruning.

table_families.primary_access_path: Existing cloud-removal API/store and provider erasure executor; parked972 is the dev predecessor, with canonical419/420 in qualification. Owner/attempt lookups bind exact review, dispatch and recovery. Read-only discovery creates no removal operation.

Completed archives are limited to 2 MiB and preserve exact resource/history digests; no content or credentials. No time-based pruning without a replacement recovery contract.
table_families.deletion_behavior: Cloud-only finalization preserves account/vault and replaces the registry with a clean unplaced identity, advancing placement epoch and retaining exact prior homes. Full account erasure explicitly removes these records only under its independent full-account tombstone. Standbys, migration jobs and unresolved earlier homes block cloud removal. Unapproved, undispatched reviews can cancel only through the atomic exact-snapshot restoration port; approval and cancellation serialize on the existing owner locks.

table_families.trust_boundary: No OAuth tokens, vault keys, filenames or file contents. Database guards bind owner, attempt, incarnation, snapshot and exact approved review. Legacy account-cleanup authorization cannot grant cloud-only purpose. Read-only inspection covers recorded owner resources only; labels and provider DELETE acceptance do not prove ownership or absence.
